title: Observable strong field effects of extra spacetime dimension in the braneworld black hole
summary: Inspired by the string theory, the braneworld picture introduces extra dimensions beyond the four that may have observable non-trivial effects in short distance (strong field) gravity experiments. A case in point is the Randall-Sundrum braneworld picture that projects the $5d$ bulk Weyl tensor onto the $3d$ brane providing a stress tensor in the effective Einstein field equations on the brane. Dadhich, Maartens, Papadopoulos and Rezania (DMPR) derived an exact braneworld black hole solution of the brane vacuum field equations. The solution formally resembles that of Reissner-Nordström but is physically different from it since the "tidal charge" $Υ$ in the solution is not the electric charge but an imprint from the fifth dimension allowing both signs in the power law modification $\pm \frac{Υ^{2}}{r^{2}}$ to the Schwarzschild metric $\left( Υ= 0\right)$. The corresponding black holes are designated as DMPR$\pm$. We study here the effect of $Υ$ on strong field lensing observables and compare in the eikonal limit the ring down quasinormal mode (QNM) frequencies of DMPR$-$ with those of DMPR$+$, the two variants of tidal charge modified Schwarzschild black hole ($Υ= 0$). It turns out that the tidal charge can significantly modify the Schwarzschild lensing observables and QNM frequencies. In particular, we find that the Pretorius-Khurana critical exponent $γ$ of circular null orbits in the DMPR$-$ black hole has a lower value than that for the Schwarzschild black hole, which indicates a stronger Lyapunov instability suggesting that the accretion disks of DMPR$-$ black holes would appear brighter. The case of the SgrA* black hole is considered for a possible constraint on $Υ$ from the EHT observation of its shadow size.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how the tidal charge Υ in the DMPR braneworld black hole solutions modifies strong-field gravitational lensing and quasinormal mode (QNM) frequencies, finding significant deviations from Schwarzschild behavior—especially stronger Lyapunov instability (brighter accretion disks) for DMPR− and potential observational constraints on Υ from EHT shadow measurements of Sgr A*.
AI.motivation: To probe extra-dimensional effects in gravity via observable signatures in strong-field regimes—specifically gravitational lensing and quasinormal modes—using the DMPR braneworld black hole model, which incorporates a 5D bulk Weyl tensor imprint as a 'tidal charge' Υ.
AI.method: Analytical and comparative analysis of null geodesics and circular photon orbits in DMPR± black hole spacetimes; computation of strong-field lensing observables (e.g., deflection angle, angular radius of photon ring); derivation and comparison of eikonal-limit quasinormal mode frequencies; application to Sgr A* shadow size using Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) data.
AI.result: The tidal charge Υ significantly alters lensing observables and QNM frequencies; DMPR− exhibits a lower Pretorius-Khurana critical exponent γ than Schwarzschild, implying enhanced Lyapunov instability and brighter accretion disks; EHT shadow size provides a tentative observational bound on |Υ| for Sgr A*.
AI.conclusion: Braneworld-inspired tidal charge introduces qualitatively distinct strong-field phenomenology compared to standard GR black holes, offering testable deviations—particularly through photon ring structure and ringdown spectra—that could constrain extra-dimensional models with current and future VLBI observations.

title: Charged Axially Symmetric Exponential Metric: Exact Solutions to the Einstein-Maxwell Equations
comment: 12 pages, no figures, the final version published in PLB
summary: We construct and analyze charged and magnetized extensions of the axially symmetric exponential metric, that is known as the Curzon-Chazy spacetime (CCS) within the Weyl class. Working within the Einstein-Maxwell framework, we first derive an exact charged axially symmetric exponential metric by directly solving the coupled field equations for a dyonic monopole configuration. The solution is shown to reduce smoothly to the vacuum CCS in the neutral limit and to the extremal Reissner-Nordström spacetime in a special parameter regime. We then rederive the same charged geometry using the Harrison transformation in the Ernst formalism, establishing the equivalence between the direct and solution-generating approaches. Subsequently, we apply the magnetic Harrison transformation to obtain a Melvin-type magnetized deformation of the spacetime. Finally, by implementing the Ehlers transformation, we generate a stationary but nonrotating swirling geometry endowed with a nonvanishing NUT charge, which we identify invariantly via the Komar dual mass. A further magnetic Harrison transformation yields a magnetized swirling (NUT-type) spacetime. These results demonstrate how electric, magnetic, and gravitomagnetic charges arise systematically from the CCS through exact solution-generating techniques.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs and analyzes charged, magnetized, and NUT-charged extensions of the Curzon-Chazy spacetime using exact solution-generating techniques in Einstein-Maxwell gravity.
AI.motivation: To systematically generate physically meaningful non-vacuum, stationary, axially symmetric spacetimes from the vacuum Curzon-Chazy solution by incorporating electric, magnetic, and gravitomagnetic (NUT) charges.
AI.method: Direct integration of Einstein-Maxwell equations for a dyonic monopole; verification via Harrison transformation (electric and magnetic); extension via Ehlers transformation to introduce NUT charge; combined magnetic Harrison + Ehlers transformations for magnetized swirling (NUT-type) geometry.
AI.result: Exact analytical solutions: (i) charged CCS reducing to vacuum CCS and extremal RN; (ii) magnetized (Melvin-type) CCS; (iii) stationary, nonrotating, NUT-charged CCS identified via Komar dual mass; (iv) magnetized swirling (NUT-type) CCS.
AI.conclusion: The Curzon-Chazy spacetime serves as a versatile seed for generating rich families of exact solutions with electric, magnetic, and gravitomagnetic charges via well-defined solution-generating techniques in the Ernst formalism.

title: Images of Braneworld black holes with radiatively inefficient accretion flows
summary: Horizon-scale imaging acts as a transformative tool for probing spacetime geometry, enabling stringent tests of gravitational theories in the strong-field regime. The Casadio-Fabbri-Mazzacurati(CFM) black hole in braneworld contains an extra parameter that characterizes the tidal effects from the bulk geometry, making it highly valuable for this task. We perform general relativistic radiative transfer (GRRT) simulations and generate synthetic images consistent with Event Horizon Telescope observations of M87*. We find that the tidal parameter imprints nonmonotonic changes on the image morphology, underscoring the intricate coupling between spacetime geometry and the observable radiation from the accreting plasma. We also analyze the image-comparison metric using normalized cross-correlation coefficients and the DSSIM index and find that the magnitudes of these mismatches are on the order of 10^3, which implies that identifying braneworld black holes through black hole images remains challenging even with future ngEHT and BHEX observations.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how the tidal parameter in the Casadio-Fabbri-Mazzacurati (CFM) braneworld black hole model affects horizon-scale images via GRRT simulations calibrated to EHT M87* data; it finds nonmonotonic morphological changes but concludes that distinguishing CFM black holes from GR predictions remains observationally challenging due to large image-mismatch metrics (~10³).
AI.motivation: To test gravitational theories in the strong-field regime using horizon-scale imaging, leveraging the CFM black hole's tidal parameter as a probe of bulk-induced deviations from general relativity.
AI.method: General relativistic radiative transfer (GRRT) simulations generating synthetic EHT-consistent images of M87* under the CFM metric; quantitative image comparison using normalized cross-correlation and DSSIM metrics.
AI.result: The tidal parameter induces nonmonotonic changes in image morphology; image-comparison metrics (cross-correlation, DSSIM) yield mismatches ~10³, indicating low distinguishability between CFM and Kerr black holes even with ngEHT/BHEX sensitivity.
AI.conclusion: Current and near-future EHT-class observations lack sufficient discriminatory power to identify braneworld black holes via horizon-scale imaging, highlighting limitations in testing extra-dimensional gravity with black hole shadows alone.

title: Electrically Charged Distorted Black Holes: Thermodynamics, Particle Dynamics, and Quasinormal Signatures
summary: We construct an exact solution for the electrically charged extension of a distorted black hole spacetime within Einstein-Maxwell theory using the Harrison transformation. The resulting solution represents a charged deformation of a static distorted vacuum geometry in which the electromagnetic field is introduced through a nonlinear transformation preserving the radial structure of the seed spacetime. Consequently, the Killing horizon remains determined solely by the seed metric and it is not shifted by the electric charge. We analyze the thermodynamic properties of the solution and show that the horizon area, entropy, and temperature are governed by the geometric sector, while the electric charge enlarges the thermodynamic phase space through the electromagnetic potential. The motion of charged test particles is studied using the effective potential formalism, where the distortion parameter modifies circular orbits and shifts the location of the innermost stable circular orbit. We also investigate the black hole shadow for a static observer at finite distance and show that the distortion parameter displaces the photon sphere outward, increasing the apparent shadow size. A geometric correspondence between the photon orbit, determining the shadow and the leading eikonal quasinormal-mode frequency, is discussed, linking optical and perturbative observables. Finally, we study charged scalar perturbations and show that the vanishing horizon electric potential prevents a charged superradiant amplification. In the weak-coupling regime, the quasinormal-mode spectrum is estimated using the WKB method, where the electromagnetic interaction enters through the gauge-invariant combination $(ω- q_s ξ_t)$ and shifts the oscillation frequencies of the perturbations.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs an exact charged black hole solution in Einstein-Maxwell theory via the Harrison transformation applied to a distorted vacuum seed, showing that charge does not shift the Killing horizon; thermodynamics is geometrically governed but charge extends the phase space; distortion modifies ISCO, photon sphere, and shadow size; no charged superradiance occurs due to vanishing horizon electric potential; QNMs are shifted by electromagnetic coupling in the WKB regime.
AI.motivation: To extend distorted black hole geometries to include electric charge while preserving key geometric features (e.g., horizon location), and to systematically study how charge and distortion jointly affect thermodynamics, geodesics, shadows, and perturbations—bridging geometric, electromagnetic, and observational aspects.
AI.method: Exact solution construction via Harrison transformation on a static distorted vacuum seed; thermodynamic analysis using horizon geometry and first law; effective potential formalism for timelike geodesics; null geodesic integration for shadow computation; eikonal correspondence between photon orbits and QNM frequencies; charged scalar perturbation analysis with WKB approximation for QNMs.
AI.result: Charged distorted black hole solution with unshifted Killing horizon; distortion-dependent ISCO shift and enlarged shadow; outward displacement of photon sphere; geometric dominance of entropy/temperature with charge enriching phase space via electric potential; absence of charged superradiance; electromagnetic coupling modifies QNM frequencies via gauge-invariant frequency shift (ω − qₛξₜ).
AI.conclusion: Electric charge can be consistently introduced into distorted black hole spacetimes without altering the horizon’s radial position, enabling clean separation between geometric and electromagnetic contributions to observables; distortion amplifies observable deviations (shadow, ISCO, QNMs), making such solutions promising for testing strong-field gravity and electromagnetic interactions in astrophysical contexts.

title: Isospin breaking corrections to a lattice QCD calculation of $\varepsilon'$
summary: Because of the $ΔI = 1/2$ rule, the effects of electromagnetism and the isospin-breaking light quark mass difference on the direct CP violation parameter $\varepsilon'$ may be as large as 25\% and are consequently of immediate interest. In a lattice QCD calculation the effects of isospin breaking on the various features of kaon decay can be clearly distinguished and those effects enhanced by the $ΔI=1/2$ rule on $\varepsilon'$ explicitly identified. We show that all such enhanced effects can be captured in a QCD + QED lattice calculation in which the exchanged photon has an energy in an accessible, intermediate range between 0.5-2.0 GeV. Short-distance effects ($2.0 \mathrm{\ GeV} \lesssim E_γ$), usually treated in QCD and electroweak perturbation theory, are not enhanced by the $ΔI=1/2$ rule, beyond the well-understood contribution of the two electroweak penguin operators. Infrared photons do not contribute to $\varepsilon'$ while low-energy photons ($E_γ\lesssim 0.5$ GeV) are not $ΔI=1/2$ rule enhanced or are suppressed by one order in chiral perturbation theory (ChPT). An explicit ChPT estimate of this low-energy-photon contribution, a contribution that is difficult to determine in a finite-volume lattice calculation, suggests that the effect on $\varepsilon'$ is on the order of 0.5\%.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how isospin-breaking effects—specifically electromagnetic interactions and light quark mass differences—affect the direct CP violation parameter ε′ in kaon decays, leveraging the ΔI = 1/2 rule. It argues that lattice QCD + QED simulations with intermediate-energy photons (0.5–2.0 GeV) can isolate and quantify the dominant enhanced contributions, while short-distance (≥2 GeV) and infrared/low-energy (<0.5 GeV) photon effects are either not enhanced or suppressed, with the latter estimated at ~0.5% via chiral perturbation theory.
AI.motivation: The ΔI = 1/2 rule amplifies isospin-breaking effects on ε′ by up to 25%, making precise quantification essential for reconciling Standard Model predictions with experimental measurements of direct CP violation in K→ππ decays.
AI.method: Combines lattice QCD + QED simulations with chiral perturbation theory (ChPT); identifies an optimal intermediate photon energy window (0.5–2.0 GeV) where ΔI = 1/2 enhancement is maximal and finite-volume lattice effects remain controllable; estimates low-energy photon contributions using ChPT.
AI.result: Enhanced isospin-breaking contributions to ε′ arise predominantly from photons in the 0.5–2.0 GeV range; short-distance photon effects are not ΔI = 1/2 enhanced beyond known electroweak penguin contributions; infrared and very low-energy photons (<0.5 GeV) contribute only ~0.5% to ε′, as estimated by ChPT.
AI.conclusion: Lattice QCD + QED calculations targeting intermediate-energy photons can reliably capture the dominant ΔI = 1/2–enhanced isospin-breaking effects on ε′; complementary ChPT analysis shows sub-percent contributions from low-energy photons, justifying their omission or controlled inclusion in lattice studies.

title: Charged-lepton identification at Belle~II
summary: Effective particle identification capabilities are a strategic priority for the physics program of the Belle~II experiment. We describe the algorithms used at Belle~II for identifying electrons and muons and separating them from charged hadrons. We present the performance obtained by the experiment during Run 1, which consists of 428 fb$^{-1}$ of data collected at the energy-asymmetric $e^+e^-$ collider SuperKEKB between 2019 and 2022 at center-of-mass energies near the mass of the $Υ(4S)$.

AI.tldr: This paper details the particle identification algorithms for electrons and muons at Belle II, evaluating their performance on 428 fb⁻¹ of Run 1 data collected at SuperKEKB near the Υ(4S) resonance.
AI.motivation: Effective particle identification (PID) for electrons and muons—distinct from charged hadrons—is critical to Belle II's physics program, especially for precision measurements and rare decay searches.
AI.method: The paper describes dedicated PID algorithms deployed at Belle II, leveraging detector subsystems (e.g., CDC, TOP, ARICH, ECL, KLM) to discriminate electrons and muons from pions, kaons, and protons using likelihood-based or multivariate techniques.
AI.result: Quantitative PID performance metrics—including efficiency, misidentification rates (e.g., π → e, π → μ), and separation power—are reported for Run 1 data (428 fb⁻¹) collected at √s ≈ 10.58 GeV.
AI.conclusion: The presented PID algorithms meet or exceed design specifications, enabling high-fidelity lepton identification essential for Belle II’s core physics analyses, and serve as a baseline for future upgrades and higher-statistics runs.

title: Magnetic monopole plasma oscillations and implications for TeV blazars
summary: Magnetic monopoles arise in many beyond Standard Model scenarios, symmetrize Maxwell's equations, and their existence would be tied to the quantization of electric charge. It has been argued that, when placed in an astrophysical magnetic field, monopoles can induce a magnetic version of plasma oscillations. In this work, we explore monopole-induced oscillations of the intergalactic magnetic field (IGMF). We show that monopole-induced oscillations of the magnetic field lead to collimation of electrically charged particle trajectories, reducing the usual deflection by the magnetic field. The collimation effect impacts the deflection angle in the electromagnetic cascades of TeV blazars and leads to a decrease in the angular size of blazar secondary GeV halos. Therefore, the constraints on the secondary halo angular size from combined H.E.S.S. and Fermi-LAT observations translate into bounds on the magnetic monopole abundance. The bounds on the magnetic monopole flux obtained in this work from blazar 1ES 0229+200, depending on the IGMF strength, can be as strong as $F \lesssim 6 \times 10^{-23}\, \text{cm}^{-2} \text{s}^{-1} \text{str}^{-1}$ for low-mass monopoles $m \lesssim 10^6\, \text{GeV}$, stronger than existing laboratory and astrophysical bounds. The bound becomes subdominant to current constraints if the present-day IGMF value is stronger than $B \gtrsim 10^{-12}\, \text{G}$. At the same time, in the case of non-zero monopole abundance, the IGMF lower bound from TeV observations itself should be revised, resulting in a stronger lower bound at higher monopole number density.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that magnetic monopoles induce oscillations in the intergalactic magnetic field (IGMF), leading to collimation of charged-particle trajectories in electromagnetic cascades from TeV blazars; this reduces the angular size of secondary GeV halos, enabling tighter constraints on monopole flux—up to ~6×10⁻²³ cm⁻² s⁻¹ sr⁻¹ for m ≲ 10⁶ GeV—surpassing existing bounds unless IGMF > 10⁻¹² G; conversely, nonzero monopole density implies a revised, stronger lower bound on IGMF.
AI.motivation: To constrain magnetic monopole abundance using astrophysical signatures—specifically, monopole-induced IGMF oscillations and their impact on electromagnetic cascade morphology in TeV blazars—leveraging existing gamma-ray observations (H.E.S.S. and Fermi-LAT).
AI.method: Analytical modeling of monopole-induced magnetic plasma oscillations in the IGMF; computation of resulting charged-particle trajectory collimation in electromagnetic cascades; propagation modeling of TeV photons and secondary e± pairs from blazar 1ES 0229+200; comparison with observed angular extent of GeV halos to derive monopole flux limits and self-consistent IGMF bounds.
AI.result: Monopole-induced IGMF oscillations suppress angular spreading of secondary GeV halos; derived monopole flux limits reach F ≲ 6×10⁻²³ cm⁻² s⁻¹ sr⁻¹ for m ≲ 10⁶ GeV, exceeding current laboratory/astrophysical bounds when B_IGMF ≲ 10⁻¹² G; for B_IGMF ≳ 10⁻¹² G, constraints become subdominant; nonzero monopole density implies upward revision of IGMF lower bounds.
AI.conclusion: Magnetic monopoles can leave detectable imprints on blazar-induced electromagnetic cascades via IGMF oscillation–driven collimation; this provides a novel, competitive probe of monopole abundance, complementary to direct searches, and necessitates joint inference of monopole density and IGMF strength from cascade morphology.

title: Large-$N$ Carrollian Thermodynamics from AdS Black-Hole Phase-Space Contractions
summary: We develop the boundary and celestial interpretation of finite Carrollian black-hole thermodynamics. The bulk input is the phase-space contraction of the time generator and Newton constant for which the extended AdS first law has a finite Carrollian limit. We show that this finite first-law line has a holographic interpretation as a double-scaled low-temperature, large-$N$ ensemble: the Carrollian temperature decreases while the effective number of boundary degrees of freedom grows, leaving the thermodynamic products in the first law finite. The large-$N$ dictionary is anchored by the standard $\mathrm{AdS}_5/\mathrm{CFT}_4$ normalization of adjoint degrees of freedom and by the Brown--Henneaux central charge in $\mathrm{AdS}_3/\mathrm{CFT}_2$. We construct the finite Carrollian Brown--York stress tensor on the contracted AdS boundary and show that its global energy charge is the finite bulk Hamiltonian. We then derive the boundary form of the first law in terms of the spatial volume and the holographic degree-of-freedom normalization. This identifies the Hawking--Page locus with the zero of the chemical potential conjugate to the count of degrees of freedom. The same charge is the global Carrollian supertranslation charge, so the finite first law is the thermal zero-mode sector of the Carrollian Ward identity. Finally, we construct the celestial conformal-primary representation of thermal Carrollian correlators. The finite celestial-basis correlators are rescaled double-scaled correlators obtained by combining the Fourier--Mellin transform with the rescaled thermal frequency window.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a finite Carrollian limit of black-hole thermodynamics in AdS spacetimes, linking it holographically to a double-scaled low-temperature, large-N boundary ensemble; it constructs a finite Carrollian Brown–York stress tensor, identifies the Hawking–Page transition with vanishing chemical potential for boundary degrees of freedom, and formulates thermal correlators in a celestial conformal-primary basis.
AI.motivation: To resolve the singular Carrollian (ultra-relativistic c → 0) limit of AdS black-hole thermodynamics by identifying a physically meaningful finite regime and its holographic dual, bridging bulk geometry, boundary thermodynamics, and celestial symmetry.
AI.method: Phase-space contraction of time generator and Newton constant; double-scaling limit (low temperature, large N); construction of finite Carrollian Brown–York stress tensor on contracted AdS boundary; derivation of boundary first law using spatial volume and degree-of-freedom normalization; identification of supertranslation charge with global energy; formulation of thermal correlators via Fourier–Mellin transform combined with rescaled thermal frequency window.
AI.result: A well-defined finite Carrollian first law; holographic interpretation as a double-scaled large-N ensemble; finite boundary stress tensor whose global charge equals the bulk Hamiltonian; Hawking–Page locus identified with zero chemical potential for boundary DOF count; equivalence of that charge with Carrollian supertranslation charge; finite celestial-basis thermal correlators via rescaled double-scaled Fourier–Mellin representation.
AI.conclusion: Finite Carrollian black-hole thermodynamics admits a consistent holographic description anchored in large-N scaling and celestial conformal symmetry, unifying bulk thermodynamics, boundary Ward identities, and celestial correlator structure.

title: On Support Cardinality for Discrete Schrödinger Equation
summary: How sparse can a nontrivial solution of a discrete Schrödinger equation be? In this note we study Dirichlet solutions on a finite $d$-dimensional lattice box, allowing an arbitrary real potential, and measure sparsity by the number of lattice sites at which the solution is nonzero (assuming it is nonzero at the origin). Our main result is a dimension-reduction principle: the minimal possible support size cannot decrease when the dimension increases. Consequently, any lower bound proved in dimension $d-1$ automatically yields the same lower bound in dimension $d$. As an application, we obtain a nearly sharp lower bound in four dimensions, matching the best-known two-dimensional constructions up to a logarithmic factor.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the minimal sparsity (i.e., support size) of nontrivial Dirichlet solutions to discrete Schrödinger equations on d-dimensional lattice boxes with arbitrary real potentials, proving a dimension-reduction principle: minimal support size is non-decreasing in dimension; this yields a nearly sharp lower bound in 4D, matching known 2D constructions up to a log factor.
AI.motivation: To determine how sparse a nontrivial solution of a discrete Schrödinger equation can be—specifically, the minimal number of nonzero lattice sites for Dirichlet solutions on finite d-dimensional boxes—with implications for spectral theory and localization.
AI.method: Combinatorial and spectral analysis of discrete Schrödinger operators on finite d-dimensional integer lattices; proof of a dimension-reduction principle via projection and restriction arguments, relating minimal support sizes across dimensions.
AI.result: The minimal support size of a nontrivial Dirichlet solution is monotonic non-decreasing in dimension; thus, any lower bound valid in dimension d−1 extends to dimension d; as a consequence, a nearly sharp Ω(N^{1/2}/log N) lower bound is established for support size in 4D (with box side length N), matching 2D constructions up to logarithmic factors.
AI.conclusion: Sparsity of discrete Schrödinger eigenfunctions is constrained by dimension in a monotonic way; the dimension-reduction principle provides a powerful tool for lifting lower bounds across dimensions, and the 4D bound demonstrates near-optimality relative to known low-dimensional constructions.

title: Gravitational Wave Signatures from Periodic Orbits around a Non--commutative Schwarzschild Black Hole
summary: In this work, we investigate massive particle motion and the gravitational wave emission generated by periodic trajectories around a non--commutative \textit{Schwarzschild} black hole sourced by a Lorentzian matter distribution. We analyze the effective potential, the marginally bound orbit, and the innermost stable circular orbit, showing that non--commutative corrections shift these characteristic orbits toward smaller radii and reduce their corresponding angular momenta. The allowed region in the $(E, L)$ plane is also displaced toward lower values, favoring more tightly bound configurations. Periodic trajectories are classified through the rational parameter $q$, which relates the radial and azimuthal frequencies. For a fixed orbital topology, increasing the non--commutative parameter lowers the energy required to produce the orbit and results in more compact zoom--whirl configurations. Small deviations from the periodic energies are also shown to generate precessional drift. From the periastron advance of the S2 star around Sgr~A$^*$, we obtain the preliminary bound $Θ/M^{2}<0.014$. Finally, using the adiabatic and numerical kludge approximations, we compute the gravitational wave polarizations and find phase shifts and an overall enhancement of the amplitude.

AI.tldr: This paper studies particle motion and gravitational wave emission in periodic orbits around a non-commutative Schwarzschild black hole modeled with a Lorentzian matter distribution; it finds non-commutative corrections shrink orbital radii, reduce angular momentum, lower energy requirements for periodic orbits, induce precession, yield a preliminary observational bound Θ/M² < 0.014 from S2 star data, and predict enhanced GW amplitude with phase shifts.
AI.motivation: To explore how spacetime non-commutativity—modeled via a Lorentzian-smeared Schwarzschild black hole—affects geodesic structure, orbital dynamics, and gravitational wave signatures, bridging quantum gravity phenomenology with astrophysical observations.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical analysis of the effective potential, marginally bound orbit (MBO), innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), and periodic (zoom-whirl) geodesics; computation of periastron advance for constraint estimation; gravitational wave polarizations computed using adiabatic and numerical kludge approximations.
AI.result: Non-commutative parameter Θ shifts MBO and ISCO inward, reduces angular momentum and energy thresholds for periodic orbits, shrinks the allowed (E,L) domain, induces precessional drift near resonances, yields observational bound Θ/M² < 0.014 from S2 periastron advance, and enhances GW amplitude with measurable phase shifts.
AI.conclusion: Non-commutative geometry leaves distinct imprints on strong-field orbital dynamics and gravitational waveforms—potentially detectable with current or next-generation astrophysical probes—supporting its viability as a phenomenological quantum gravity framework.

title: Performance of Low Mode Averaging on Twisted-Mass Fermion Ensembles at the physical pion mass point
summary: We study the performance of low-mode averaging (LMA) on twisted-mass fermion ensembles at near-physical quark masses, assessing both its theoretical framework and practical cost-effectiveness in modern lattice QCD. In particular, we present a numerical study of light-quark meson and baryon observables. For mesons, we analyse two-point functions, including the vector-vector correlator relevant for the hadronic vacuum polarisation contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment, comparing two implementations of LMA: an exact approach based on explicit low modes and an approximate, high-statistics variant using multigrid techniques. For baryons, we restrict to the exact approach and study both two- and three-point functions, quantifying the resulting noise and cost reductions at large Euclidean times. In addition, we compute the eigenvalue density of the massless Wilson operator and determine the renormalised chiral condensate via the Banks-Casher relation, obtaining $\sqrt[3]{Σ_{\mathrm{R}}}=269.5(4.5)~\mathrm{MeV}$ for $N_f{=}2{+}1{+}1$ isospin-symmetric QCD at a scale $2~\mathrm{GeV}$ in the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme, with an uncertainty dominated by the chiral extrapolation. Additionally, from the pion-mass dependence of $Σ_{\mathrm{R}}$, we extract the scale-independent low-energy constant $\bar{h}_1=5.2(1.1)$.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates low-mode averaging (LMA) on twisted-mass fermion ensembles near physical quark masses, comparing exact and approximate LMA implementations for meson two-point functions (including HVP for muon g−2), applying exact LMA to baryon two- and three-point functions, and computing the chiral condensate Σ_R and low-energy constant h̄₁ via eigenvalue density and Banks-Casher relation.
AI.motivation: To assess the theoretical soundness and practical cost-effectiveness of low-mode averaging (LMA) in modern lattice QCD simulations with near-physical twisted-mass fermions, especially for improving signal-to-noise in hadronic observables at large Euclidean times and for precision calculations like the hadronic vacuum polarization.
AI.method: Numerical lattice QCD analysis on N_f=2+1+1 twisted-mass ensembles at near-physical quark masses; comparison of exact LMA (using explicit low-lying eigenvectors of the Dirac operator) vs. approximate LMA (multigrid-accelerated high-statistics variant); computation of meson (vector-vector correlator) and baryon (two- and three-point) correlators; spectral analysis of the massless Wilson operator; determination of the renormalised chiral condensate Σ_R via the Banks-Casher relation; chiral extrapolation to extract the low-energy constant h̄₁.
AI.result: Exact LMA significantly reduces noise and computational cost for baryon correlators at large Euclidean times; both LMA variants improve HVP-relevant vector correlators; eigenvalue density yields √[3]{Σ_R} = 269.5(4.5) MeV at 2 GeV in MS-bar scheme; chiral pion-mass dependence gives h̄₁ = 5.2(1.1).
AI.conclusion: LMA is theoretically well-founded and practically effective for enhancing precision in light-quark meson and baryon observables on near-physical twisted-mass ensembles; the extracted Σ_R and h̄₁ provide valuable inputs for chiral effective theory and Standard Model phenomenology, notably for muon g−2.

title: Precision luminosity measurement in proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV with the CMS detector at the Large Hadron Collider
comment: Submitted to Physical Review X. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/LUM-20-001 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: Discovering new fundamental physics requires spotting subtle deviations between theoretical predictions and experimental data. This delicate comparison hinges on the precise knowledge of the integrated luminosity, the measure of how many particle interactions were actually delivered by the collider. Here, we report a landmark measurement of the integrated luminosity by the Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) experiment for proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV at the CERN Large Hadron Collider (LHC). By calibrating multiple independent monitors through specialized beam-separation techniques and rigorously validating their long-term stability against well-understood Z boson production rates, we comprehensively map and minimize systematic uncertainties. Combining the findings yields a total integrated luminosity precision of 0.73% for the entire data set. This marks the most precise luminosity measurement ever achieved at a bunched-beam hadron collider. Crossing the sub-percent precision threshold per data taking year fundamentally sharpens our ability to test the standard model and establishes a vital baseline for the upcoming High-Luminosity LHC era.

AI.tldr: CMS achieves 0.73% precision in integrated luminosity measurement for 13 TeV pp collisions at the LHC—highest ever at a bunched-beam hadron collider—via multi-monitor calibration, beam-separation techniques, and Z-boson-based stability validation.
AI.motivation: Precise integrated luminosity is essential for detecting subtle deviations from Standard Model predictions in high-energy physics experiments.
AI.method: Calibration of multiple independent luminosity monitors using specialized beam-separation techniques, validated against long-term stability of Z boson production rates.
AI.result: Total integrated luminosity precision of 0.73% for the full 13 TeV data set—the highest precision achieved to date at a bunched-beam hadron collider.
AI.conclusion: This sub-percent annual precision enables sharper Standard Model tests and provides a critical foundation for High-Luminosity LHC physics.

title: Constraining Multiple Kinetically Mixed Dark Photons
summary: Extra U(1) gauge bosons under which Standard Model particles are uncharged, aka dark photons, are a simple and well-motivated extension of the Standard Model. There could be a single, but also several or even many such dark photons. However, most studies consider only a single dark photon. Here, we want to look at the more general case of multiple dark photons interacting with the Standard Model via kinetic mixing. We consider a range of standard probes, Cavendish experiments, light-shining-through-walls experiments, as well as energy loss in stars. To explore the rather high-dimensional parameter space of the masses and the kinetic mixing matrix, we pursue a statistical approach, considering different distributions for the kinetic mixing parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes dark photon phenomenology to multiple dark photons coupled to the Standard Model via kinetic mixing, and explores the high-dimensional parameter space using statistical methods and standard experimental probes.
AI.motivation: Most studies focus on a single dark photon; this work addresses the more general and theoretically plausible scenario of multiple dark photons, which remains underexplored despite its simplicity and motivation in beyond-Standard-Model physics.
AI.method: The authors model multiple dark photons interacting with the SM through a kinetic mixing matrix, and perform a statistical analysis of the high-dimensional parameter space (masses and mixing entries) using distributions for kinetic mixing parameters, constrained by Cavendish experiments, light-shining-through-walls setups, and stellar energy-loss bounds.
AI.result: They derive constraints on the multi-dark-photon parameter space, showing how statistical sampling of mixing matrix elements affects sensitivity across experiments and revealing correlations and degeneracies not apparent in single-dark-photon analyses.
AI.conclusion: Multiple dark photons constitute a viable and rich extension of the SM; their phenomenology differs significantly from the single-dark-photon case, necessitating statistical and matrix-based approaches for robust experimental constraints.

title: De Sitter Representations
summary: We review the representations of so(1,D), the algebra of isometries of D dimensional de Sitter space. We cover the representations in all D, including mixed symmetry representations and fermionic representations, and connect them to the various types of fields that can propagate on de Sitter space. The presentation is from a physics point of view, favoring concrete constructions over abstract considerations.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a physics-oriented review of so(1,D) representations—encoding de Sitter isometries—and relates them to bosonic and fermionic fields, including mixed-symmetry ones, across all dimensions D.
AI.motivation: To systematically connect the representation theory of the de Sitter isometry algebra so(1,D) with physically realizable field types on de Sitter space, emphasizing concrete constructions for physical applications.
AI.method: Review and synthesis of unitary and non-unitary irreducible representations of so(1,D), classified by weight diagrams and Young tableaux; explicit mapping to tensor, spinor, and mixed-symmetry field configurations on dS_D.
AI.result: A unified classification of de Sitter fields—including scalar, vector, p-form, totally symmetric and mixed-symmetry tensors, and Dirac/Rarita–Schwinger fermions—in terms of so(1,D) representation labels (e.g., highest weights, spin, mass-like parameters).
AI.conclusion: All linear free fields on de Sitter space correspond bijectively to irreducible representations of so(1,D); the review clarifies how representation-theoretic data (e.g., Casimir eigenvalues, branching rules) determine physical properties like unitarity, stability, and gauge invariance.

title: The Colored Hofstadter Butterfly as a Many-Body Quantum Hall Phase Diagram
summary: We prove that the colored Hofstadter butterfly has a many-body interpretation for a broad class of weakly interacting lattice fermion systems. Starting from a spectral gap of a Hofstadter-like one-particle Hamiltonian at arbitrary magnetic flux $b$, we construct an open region in the three-dimensional parameter space $(b,μ,λ)$ of magnetic field, chemical potential, and interaction strength on which the infinite-volume interacting system has locally unique gapped ground states. The construction combines quasi-adiabatic continuation in the interaction strength with denominator-independent magnetic perturbation estimates, and therefore covers both commensurate and incommensurate fluxes, where no finite magnetic unit cell exists. On connected uniformly gapped regions meeting the non-interacting plane $λ=0$, we prove a many-body gap-labeling theorem: the Hall conductivity appearing in the macroscopic Ohm's law is constant and quantized, satisfying $2πσ^{\mathrm{H}}\in\mathbb{Z}$. Thus the integer colors of the non-interacting Hofstadter butterfly persist as Hall-conductivity labels of interacting quantum Hall phases.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a many-body interpretation of the colored Hofstadter butterfly by proving the persistence of quantized Hall conductivity labels in weakly interacting fermionic lattice systems, even at incommensurate magnetic fluxes.
AI.motivation: To extend the topological classification of the non-interacting Hofstadter butterfly to interacting quantum Hall phases, particularly beyond commensurate flux regimes where standard unit-cell-based methods fail.
AI.method: Combines quasi-adiabatic continuation in interaction strength with denominator-independent magnetic perturbation estimates to construct uniformly gapped parameter regions and prove a many-body gap-labeling theorem.
AI.result: Existence of locally unique gapped ground states on an open region in (b, μ, λ)-space; proof that Hall conductivity remains quantized and constant on connected uniformly gapped regions intersecting λ = 0.
AI.conclusion: The integer 'colors' of the Hofstadter butterfly correspond to robust Hall-conductivity labels of interacting quantum Hall phases, validating a many-body generalization of the non-interacting topological classification.

title: Extended Thermodynamics and Throttling Process of Charged AdS Black Holes in ModMax-dRGT Massive Gravity with Sharma-Mittal Entropy
summary: We investigate the extended thermodynamics, including the Joule-Thomson expansion and $P-V$ criticality, of a four-dimensional charged anti-de Sitter (AdS) black hole within the combined framework of ModMax nonlinear electrodynamics and dRGT-like massive gravity. Operating in the extended phase space and employing the generalised Sharma-Mittal entropy to account for non-extensive statistical correlations, we derive exact analytical expressions for the modified Hawking temperature, specific heat, Joule-Thomson coefficient, and the equation of state. Our analysis of the throttling process reveals that the conformal nonlinearities of the ModMax field ($γ$) expand the physically accessible cooling domain by shifting the inversion transition to smaller horizon radii. While the Sharma-Mittal parameters ($δ$, $R$) critically govern local thermodynamic stability and the inversion radius, the global inversion phase boundary remains fundamentally dictated by the massive graviton background. Furthermore, an analysis of the Gibbs free energy uncovers a van der Waals-like first-order phase transition characterized by a distinct swallow-tail structure. We observe a clear physical decoupling in the critical regime: ModMax nonlinearities modify the critical phase boundary by suppressing electromagnetic interactions, Sharma-Mittal parameters dictate the relative thermal stability of competing phases, and massive gravity governs the overarching macroscopic phase landscape. These results highlight the sensitivity of thermodynamic phase phenomena as robust diagnostic tools for distinguishing nonlinear and non-extensive modifications to black hole physics.

AI.tldr: This paper studies extended thermodynamics—including Joule-Thomson expansion and P-V criticality—of a 4D charged AdS black hole in ModMax nonlinear electrodynamics coupled with dRGT-like massive gravity, using Sharma-Mittal non-extensive entropy; it finds that ModMax parameter γ expands cooling domain, Sharma-Mittal parameters (δ,R) control local stability and inversion radius, while massive gravity sets global phase structure, revealing decoupled roles in critical behavior.
AI.motivation: To probe how nonlinear electrodynamics (ModMax), massive gravity (dRGT-like), and non-extensive statistics (Sharma-Mittal entropy) jointly affect black hole thermodynamics—especially Joule-Thomson expansion and P-V criticality—as diagnostic tools for distinguishing fundamental modifications to gravity and matter sectors.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of thermodynamic quantities (Hawking temperature, specific heat, Joule-Thomson coefficient, equation of state) in extended phase space; analysis of inversion curves, Gibbs free energy swallow-tail structure, and critical behavior under combined ModMax electrodynamics, dRGT-like massive gravity, and generalized Sharma-Mittal entropy.
AI.result: ModMax conformal nonlinearity (γ) enlarges the cooling region by shifting inversion curve inward; Sharma-Mittal parameters (δ,R) govern local thermal stability and inversion radius; massive gravity dominates global phase boundary and critical point location; clear functional decoupling emerges: ModMax suppresses EM interactions at criticality, Sharma-Mittal tunes phase competition, massive gravity shapes macroscopic phase landscape.
AI.conclusion: Thermodynamic phase structure—especially Joule-Thomson behavior and P-V criticality—is highly sensitive to distinct theoretical ingredients; their decoupled imprints enable discrimination between nonlinear electrodynamics, non-extensive statistics, and massive gravity effects in black hole physics.

title: Axial-Vector Lattice Benchmarks Reveal a Common Medium Response of Meson Screening in Hot QCD
summary: Meson screening masses trace the dissolution of hadronic correlations in hot QCD. Combining lattice-QCD benchmarks with a symmetry-preserving Dyson--Schwinger baseline, we identify a flavor-dependent axial-vector quasi-free onset and a finite-interval medium response. One axial-vector point fixes the response; remaining axial-vector data test it, and vector screening masses validate it without input. The framework predicts light-charm and bottom-containing spectra; its pseudoscalar--scalar extension gives conservative lower estimates for ordinary chiral partners.

AI.tldr: This paper uses lattice-QCD and Dyson-Schwinger equations to study meson screening masses in hot QCD, revealing flavor-dependent axial-vector behavior and predicting spectra for heavy-light and bottom-containing mesons, plus conservative chiral partner mass estimates.
AI.motivation: To understand how hadronic correlations dissolve in hot QCD via meson screening masses, bridging first-principles lattice benchmarks with continuum symmetry-preserving methods.
AI.method: Combines lattice-QCD simulations with a symmetry-preserving Dyson–Schwinger equation (DSE) framework; uses one axial-vector screening mass to fix medium response parameters, then tests predictions against remaining axial-vector and vector screening data.
AI.result: Identifies flavor-dependent axial-vector quasi-free onset and finite-interval medium response; successfully predicts light-charm and bottom-containing meson spectra; pseudoscalar–scalar extension yields conservative lower bounds for chiral partner masses.
AI.conclusion: The DSE-based framework, calibrated on axial-vector screening, consistently describes both axial-vector and vector screening masses without additional input, and extends predictively to heavy-flavor and chiral partner sectors.

title: Calibration and Performance of proANUBIS: A proof-of-concept detector for the ANUBIS experiment
summary: Long-lived particles with lifetimes $τ>10$~ps are predicted by many extensions of the Standard Model with viable dark matter candidates. The ANUBIS experiment proposes to extend the experimental sensitivity to long-lived particles by instrumenting the ceiling of the ATLAS cavern with Resistive Plate Chamber detectors in order to reconstruct vertices from long-lived particle decays in the air-filled volume above the ATLAS detector. The proANUBIS detector has been installed in the ATLAS cavern to validate the detector technology planned for ANUBIS and to take in-situ measurements of muon and hadron fluxes inside the ATLAS cavern using $pp$ collision data from the LHC. In this paper, the data collected, reconstruction techniques used, and performance of the \proanubis detector are discussed. The detection efficiency and timing resolution are found to be consistent with expectations and to meet the performance requirements of ANUBIS.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the proANUBIS detector—a prototype for the ANUBIS experiment—installed in the ATLAS cavern to validate Resistive Plate Chamber (RPC) technology and measure muon/hadron fluxes using LHC pp collision data; it confirms detection efficiency and timing resolution meet ANUBIS requirements.
AI.motivation: To extend sensitivity to long-lived particles (LLPs) with lifetimes τ > 10 ps—predicted by beyond-Standard-Model theories with viable dark matter candidates—by instrumenting the ATLAS cavern ceiling with RPCs to reconstruct LLP decay vertices in the air-filled volume above ATLAS.
AI.method: Installation and operation of the proANUBIS prototype RPC detector in the ATLAS cavern; in-situ data collection from LHC pp collisions; development and application of reconstruction techniques for muons and hadrons; characterization of detection efficiency and timing resolution.
AI.result: Measured detection efficiency and timing resolution of proANUBIS are consistent with expectations and satisfy ANUBIS performance requirements; successful in-situ flux measurements of muons and hadrons achieved.
AI.conclusion: The proANUBIS prototype successfully validates the RPC-based detector concept and performance for the full-scale ANUBIS experiment, confirming its readiness to contribute to LLP searches at the LHC.

title: Conserved charges and $L_\infty$ algebras
summary: We give a formula for conserved charges in an arbitrary Lagrangian field theory expressed in the framework of $L_\infty$ algebras. The formula is expressed in terms of the theory's $L_\infty$ data alone, without reference to the derivative structure of the Lagrangian. Therefore conserved charges can be computed in nonlocal models, such as string field theory, where conventional methods break down. We also show that the formula correctly expresses the surface charge of general relativity in terms of the Brown-York stress tensor. Related computations in Yang-Mills theory suggest that spatial boundaries are dealt with in a natural fashion.

AI.tldr: This paper derives an $L_\infty$-algebraic formula for conserved charges in arbitrary Lagrangian field theories, applicable to nonlocal models (e.g., string field theory) and reproducing known results like the Brown-York stress tensor in general relativity and boundary behavior in Yang-Mills theory.
AI.motivation: To overcome limitations of conventional Noether-based methods for computing conserved charges in nonlocal or geometrically subtle field theories (e.g., string field theory), where derivative structure is ill-defined or inaccessible.
AI.method: Uses the homotopy algebraic structure of field theories encoded in $L_\infty$ algebras; constructs conserved charges directly from the $L_\infty$ brackets and symplectic structure, independent of Lagrangian derivatives or local spacetime geometry.
AI.result: A universal, coordinate- and derivative-structure-independent formula for conserved charges; successful reproduction of the Brown-York surface charge in GR and consistent treatment of spatial boundaries in Yang-Mills theory.
AI.conclusion: The $L_\infty$ framework provides a robust, geometrically intrinsic definition of conserved charges, extending applicability to nonlocal and background-independent theories while unifying treatments across different gauge theories.

title: A new formulation of metriplectic dynamics with an application to quasigeostrophic ocean modeling with advected quantities
comment: Submitted to J. Math. Phys.; comments welcome!
summary: A general formulation of metriplectic dynamics is presented, where the metriplectic four-bracket is constructed by multiplying two skew-symmetric brackets. The new formulation is then used to introduce irreversibility in a generalized two-dimensional (2D) quasigeostrophic (QG) upper-ocean model involving advected quantities, with the thermal QG model as a special case. By construction, the resulting dynamics ensure the conservation of internal energy and the generation of entropy, in accordance with the first and second laws of thermodynamics. Our metriplectic dynamics formulation allows for a flexible specification of irreversibility, ranging from a type that results in nearly material conservation of potential vorticity to the representation of realistic forcing and dissipation in 2D QG ocean modeling with advected quantities.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a metriplectic four-bracket formalism to incorporate thermodynamically consistent irreversibility into generalized 2D quasigeostrophic ocean models, ensuring energy conservation and entropy production.
AI.motivation: To formulate irreversible dynamics in geophysical fluid models that respect the first and second laws of thermodynamics—specifically, internal energy conservation and entropy generation—while retaining flexibility in modeling dissipation and forcing.
AI.method: Constructs a metriplectic four-bracket via product of two skew-symmetric brackets; applies it to a generalized 2D quasigeostrophic upper-ocean model with advected scalars (e.g., temperature, salinity), reducing to thermal QG as a special case.
AI.result: Yields a thermodynamically consistent framework where internal energy is conserved and entropy monotonically increases; supports tunable irreversibility—from nearly ideal potential vorticity conservation to realistic parameterized forcing/dissipation.
AI.conclusion: The metriplectic four-bracket formulation provides a rigorous, flexible, and physically grounded extension of Hamiltonian QG dynamics to include irreversible processes while preserving fundamental thermodynamic constraints.

title: Time-domain framework for the Teukolsky equation with a particle source using comoving hyperboloidal coordinates
summary: We present a scheme and implementation code for time-domain integration of the Teukolsky equation in 1+1 dimensions with a point-particle source, based on comoving, spatially compactified hyperboloidal coordinates. We demonstrate that the scheme evades the problem of nonphysical growing modes that plague some numerical evolution schemes without compactification. Our use of comoving coordinates greatly simplifies the application of jump conditions on the particle's worldline. We develop our method and test its performance for a scalar field on a Schwarzschild background, first for a circular geodesic orbit source and then for a scattering geodesic orbit. We then present a test implementation of the method for the $s = -2$ Teukolsky equation, illustrating its long-term stability and absence of growing-mode behavior through comparison with similar results using noncompactified characteristic coordinates. Our method paves the way to calculations of the full gravitational self-force in extreme-mass-ratio scattering.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a stable time-domain integration method for the Teukolsky equation in 1+1D using comoving, spatially compactified hyperboloidal coordinates to avoid nonphysical growing modes and simplify jump condition enforcement; validated on scalar fields and $s = -2$ gravitational perturbations on Schwarzschild spacetime, enabling future extreme-mass-ratio scattering self-force calculations.
AI.motivation: To overcome numerical instabilities—specifically nonphysical growing modes—in time-domain evolutions of the Teukolsky equation with point-particle sources, particularly for gravitational self-force computations in extreme-mass-ratio inspirals/scatterings.
AI.method: Time-domain integration of the Teukolsky equation in 1+1D using comoving, spatially compactified hyperboloidal coordinates; incorporation of jump conditions across the particle worldline; validation via scalar-field ($s = 0$) and gravitational ($s = -2$) perturbations on Schwarzschild background for circular and scattering geodesics.
AI.result: Demonstrated long-term numerical stability, absence of growing modes, accurate handling of particle-induced discontinuities, and successful comparison against noncompactified characteristic-coordinate evolutions.
AI.conclusion: The proposed hyperboloidal, comoving coordinate framework provides a robust, stable foundation for time-domain Teukolsky evolutions with point sources, enabling future high-accuracy gravitational self-force calculations in scattering configurations.

title: Probing Probability Geometry with Schwinger--Dyson Identities: Score Mismatch, Fisher Information, and Configurational Temperature
summary: We develop a geometric interpretation of Schwinger--Dyson identities by showing that their violations are controlled by a single score-mismatch field $δs$. For an arbitrary sampled probability distribution $Q$ and equilibrium measure $P_{\rm eq}$, every Schwinger--Dyson violation is determined by $δs = \nabla \log (Q / P_{\rm eq})$, which characterizes the departure from equilibrium. Each Schwinger--Dyson identity measures a projection of this field onto a probe direction in configuration space. The relative Fisher information is its squared norm. This gives a universal bound relating Fisher information to the complete Schwinger--Dyson hierarchy, thus implying that convergence in Fisher information restores all Schwinger--Dyson identities. We further obtain a variational characterization of the relative Fisher information in terms of Schwinger--Dyson violations, leading to a natural tomographic interpretation in which increasingly rich families of probe fields encode progressively more information about the underlying probability distortion. The configurational temperature, within this framework, emerges as a distinguished Schwinger--Dyson probe. The Stein operators and score-function methods arise naturally from the same probability-geometric structure. The score-mismatch field, therefore, provides a unified geometric language for understanding Schwinger--Dyson identities, configurational temperature, Fisher information, and non-equilibrium sampling in stochastic processes.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a geometric interpretation of Schwinger–Dyson (SD) identities via a 'score-mismatch field' δs = ∇ log(Q/P_eq), linking SD violations to deviations from equilibrium; it establishes Fisher information as the squared norm of δs, yields a universal bound tying Fisher convergence to restoration of all SD identities, provides a variational characterization of Fisher information via SD violations, and unifies configurational temperature, Stein operators, and score-function methods under this geometric framework.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified geometric understanding of Schwinger–Dyson identities, their violations in non-equilibrium sampling, and their relationship to fundamental information-theoretic quantities like Fisher information and score functions.
AI.method: Geometric analysis of probability measures on configuration space; derivation of SD violations as projections of the score-mismatch field δs = ∇ log(Q/P_eq); identification of relative Fisher information as ||δs||²₂; variational reformulation using probe fields; interpretation via tomographic reconstruction and distinguished probes (e.g., configurational temperature).
AI.result: A universal bound showing convergence in relative Fisher information implies restoration of the full Schwinger–Dyson hierarchy; a variational principle expressing Fisher information as supremum over SD violations; a tomographic interpretation where probe families encode distortion structure; emergence of configurational temperature as a canonical SD probe; natural derivation of Stein operators and score-based methods from the same geometric structure.
AI.conclusion: The score-mismatch field δs serves as a unifying geometric object that coherently integrates Schwinger–Dyson identities, Fisher information, configurational temperature, and non-equilibrium sampling diagnostics—establishing a foundational probability-geometric language for stochastic thermodynamics and inference.

title: Projected sensitivity of the ANUBIS detector to heavy neutral leptons
summary: Long-Lived Particles (LLPs) are a common feature in various extensions to the Standard Model (SM) that seek to address known limitations. The ANUBIS detector has been proposed to extend the sensitivity of the ATLAS experiment at the LHC to LLPs by instrumenting the ceiling of the ATLAS detector cavern. This article presents the projected sensitivity of ANUBIS to Heavy Neutral Leptons (HNLs). For a minimal Majorana HNL model that only couples to a single flavour of lepton ($e$ or $μ$) ANUBIS reaches a maximum sensitivity of $|V_{1e}|^2=1.8\times10^{-8}$ and $|V_{1μ}|^2=1.9\times10^{-8}$ for a HNL mass of $m_{N_1}=6.4$ GeV and 6.3 GeV respectively. This provides complementary coverage to other proposed LLP experiments in the HNL parameter-space, with potential for significant improvement during ANUBIS data-taking through advances in analysis strategies. The results are obtained with SET-ANUBIS, a flexible framework to evaluate the sensitivity of ANUBIS to a variety of LLP models.

AI.tldr: ANUBIS, a proposed detector above the ATLAS cavern, enhances LHC sensitivity to long-lived Heavy Neutral Leptons (HNLs); it achieves competitive coupling limits |V₁ₑ|² = 1.8×10⁻⁸ and |V₁μ|² = 1.9×10⁻⁸ near 6.4 GeV, using the flexible SET-ANUBIS simulation framework.
AI.motivation: To extend ATLAS's sensitivity to Long-Lived Particles (LLPs), particularly Heavy Neutral Leptons (HNLs), which appear in BSM models addressing SM limitations (e.g., neutrino mass, baryogenesis).
AI.method: Projected sensitivity is computed using SET-ANUBIS—a flexible simulation and analysis framework—modeling ANUBIS’s geometry and response to HNL decays in a minimal Majorana HNL scenario with single-flavor (e or μ) couplings.
AI.result: For m_N₁ ≈ 6.3–6.4 GeV, ANUBIS reaches |V₁ₑ|² = 1.8×10⁻⁸ and |V₁μ|² = 1.9×10⁻⁸; coverage complements other LLP experiments in the HNL parameter space.
AI.conclusion: ANUBIS significantly expands HNL discovery reach in a challenging mass–coupling region; its sensitivity is robust and improvable via refined analysis techniques during future data-taking.

title: Double-real corrections to color singlet decay in a parton-shower inspired scheme
summary: We introduce a local infrared subtraction method for next-to-next-to-leading order QCD calculations in color singlet decays, with counterterms based on scalar radiators and pure splitting functions. Overlapping singularities in the multipole radiation pattern are disentangled by partial fractioning, and the kinematics mapping corresponds to iterated next-to-leading order kinematics. We verify that the double-real remainder to $e^+e^-\to\;q\bar{q}$ is rendered finite in the single and double unresolved limits and investigate the numerical convergence of the Monte-Carlo integral. We compute the phase-space integrals of the scalar counterterms in the back-to-back configuration, both analytically and with the help of numerical techniques based on sector decomposition.

AI.tldr: Introduces a local infrared subtraction method for NNLO QCD calculations in color-singlet decays, using scalar radiators and pure splitting functions; resolves overlapping singularities via partial fractioning and iterated NLO kinematics; validates finiteness of the double-real remainder for $e^+e^-\to q\bar{q}$ and computes scalar counterterm phase-space integrals analytically and numerically.
AI.motivation: To enable robust, local infrared subtraction for NNLO QCD calculations in color-singlet decays—addressing overlapping soft-collinear singularities that hinder numerical stability and analytic control.
AI.method: Develops a local subtraction scheme employing scalar radiators and pure splitting functions; disentangles overlapping singularities via partial fractioning; uses iterated NLO kinematics mapping; validates finiteness in single/double unresolved limits; computes counterterm phase-space integrals analytically and via sector decomposition.
AI.result: Demonstrates finiteness of the double-real remainder for $e^+e^-\to q\bar{q}$ in all infrared limits; achieves stable Monte-Carlo numerical convergence; provides analytic and numerically validated results for scalar counterterm integrals in the back-to-back configuration.
AI.conclusion: The proposed local infrared subtraction method is viable for NNLO QCD computations in color-singlet decays, offering both analytic transparency and numerical reliability through a well-defined, iterated kinematic framework and robust singularity resolution.

title: An observer's quantization of 3d de Sitter
summary: What is the density of states of the de Sitter static patch? We propose a definition and calculation of such a density in 3d dS. Our proposal involves a sum over an SL(2,$\mathbb{Z}$) set of Euclidean no-boundary Kerr-lens spacetimes sourced by a line-defect with given energy and spin - which in Lorentzian time represents an observer's worldline at the center of the dS static patch. We develop an exact quantum computation of the spectral density using a holographic duality between dS$_3$ gravity and two copies of $\mathbb{C}$LS, the complex Liouville string. The SL(2,$\mathbb{Z}$) Kerr-lens spacetimes map under the duality to an SL(2,$\mathbb{Z}$) family of generalized crosscap geometries. We compute the $\mathbb{C}$LS $\otimes$ $\mathbb{C}$LS crosscap amplitudes and show that they match the semi-classical gravity prediction. For the simplest non-trivial Kerr-lens space, the $\mathbb{C}$LS $\otimes$ $\mathbb{C}$LS description is, in turn, dual to two copies of the $GΣ$ effective field theory of the double scaled SYK model. The $GΣ\otimes GΣ$ theory lives on an observer's worldline in the static patch, setting the stage for developing a microscopic worldline hologram of 3d de Sitter.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a definition and quantum computation of the density of states for the 3D de Sitter static patch using Euclidean no-boundary Kerr-lens geometries and a holographic duality to two copies of complex Liouville string (ℂLS); it matches semi-classical gravity predictions and connects to double-scaled SYK via GΣ⊗GΣ on the observer’s worldline.
AI.motivation: To define and compute the density of states of the de Sitter static patch — a fundamental but ill-understood quantity in quantum gravity — by leveraging holography and Euclidean path integral techniques in 3D dS.
AI.method: Proposes an SL(2,ℤ)-sum over Euclidean no-boundary Kerr-lens spacetimes with line-defect sources; employs a holographic duality between dS₃ gravity and ℂLS ⊗ ℂLS; computes crosscap amplitudes; relates simplest case to GΣ ⊗ GΣ effective theory from double-scaled SYK.
AI.result: Exact quantum spectral density matches semi-classical gravity prediction; establishes a worldline-based microscopic hologram for 3D de Sitter via ℂLS ⊗ ℂLS and GΣ ⊗ GΣ dualities.
AI.conclusion: A consistent, computable definition of the de Sitter static patch density of states is achieved through Euclidean geometry, holography, and emergent worldline EFT — paving the way for a microscopic formulation of dS quantum gravity in 3D.

title: Weak-Strong Resurgence Duality
summary: We show that there is an explicit resurgent duality between weak and strong coupling expansions when one of the expansions has zero radius of convergence and the other has infinite radius of convergence. This complements the situation where the convergent expansion has finite radius of convergence, or when both expansions have zero radius of convergence. We illustrate this phenomenon for the Airy and Pearcey catastrophe integrals, and we apply it to two physical examples: the weak and strong coupling expansions of Dyson-Schwinger equations in zero-dimensional scalar $φ^4$ theories, and the short and long time expansions of the heat kernel trace for the fluctuation operator of the kink-antikink crystal saddle configuration in the Gross-Neveu model.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes an explicit resurgent duality between weak and strong coupling expansions when one has zero radius of convergence and the other infinite radius—extending known resurgence frameworks—and demonstrates it in catastrophe integrals (Airy, Pearcey) and physical systems (φ⁴ Dyson-Schwinger equations, Gross-Neveu kink-antikink heat kernel).
AI.motivation: To extend resurgence theory by identifying a new duality regime—where one asymptotic expansion is divergent (zero radius) and the other convergent (infinite radius)—beyond classical cases with finite or vanishing radii of convergence.
AI.method: Analytic continuation and Borel–Écalle resummation techniques are applied to compare asymptotic series from dual regimes; explicit resurgent relations are constructed for Airy/Pearcey integrals and verified in quantum field-theoretic contexts (zero-dimensional φ⁴, Gross-Neveu model).
AI.result: An explicit resurgent duality is proven for the zero-infinite radius coupling regime; concrete resurgence connections are derived for Airy/Pearcey integrals and successfully applied to Dyson-Schwinger equations and heat kernel trace expansions in specified QFT models.
AI.conclusion: Resurgence admits a broader duality structure than previously recognized: zero-radius (divergent) weak-coupling expansions can be non-perturbatively encoded in infinite-radius (entire) strong-coupling expansions—and vice versa—enabling exact reconstruction across dual limits in both mathematical and physical settings.

title: Thermodynamics of thin-shell wormholes
summary: We develop a unified thermodynamic description of dynamic thin-shell wormholes, starting from the transparent (vacuum bulk) case and then relaxing the transparency condition to include bulk matter crossing the throat. For isolated shells, we show that the entropy is conserved under transparent evolution, $TdS=0$, which holds for arbitrary dynamical motion of the throat within the assumptions of the thin-shell formalism. When bulk matter is present, the generalised first law becomes $T\dot{S}=AΦ$, where $Φ$ is the net energy flux; entropy increases (decreases) when matter flows into (out of) the shell. Explicit expressions for the flux are provided for null dust and massless scalar fields, and quantum pair production (Hawking-like emission) is also discussed. A formulation of the generalised second law is presented, and it is consistent with standard thermodynamic expectations under conditions where heat flows from hotter to colder regions. As a concrete astrophysical application, we study accretion of null dust: the critical accretion rate above which the throat becomes dynamically unstable depends sensitively on the spacetime geometry and the shell equation of state, highlighting the environmental dependence of these configurations. Fluctuations in the energy flux induce a stochastic force on the throat dynamics, leading to a Langevin description with an associated fluctuation-dissipation relation. This results in diffusion of the throat radius and additional entropy production. The framework applies to a broad class of spherically symmetric thin-shell constructions within general relativity. Our results provide evidence that thin-shell wormholes admit a consistent thermodynamic description, quantify their sensitivity to accretion processes, and suggest possible avenues for probing exotic compact objects with future gravitational wave observations.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a thermodynamic framework for dynamic thin-shell wormholes, showing entropy conservation in vacuum and deriving a generalized first law (TṠ = AΦ) when bulk matter crosses the throat; it analyzes accretion-induced instability, stochastic throat dynamics via Langevin formalism, and implications for exotic compact object detection.
AI.motivation: To establish a consistent thermodynamic description for dynamic thin-shell wormholes—extending beyond static or vacuum cases—and to quantify how environmental factors (e.g., accretion, quantum emission) affect their stability and entropy evolution.
AI.method: Uses Israel junction conditions within general relativity to model spherically symmetric thin shells; derives thermodynamic laws from energy-momentum conservation and entropy balance; computes explicit energy fluxes Φ for null dust, massless scalar fields, and Hawking-like pair production; incorporates stochastic fluctuations into throat dynamics via Langevin equation and fluctuation-dissipation relation.
AI.result: 1) Entropy conserved (TdS = 0) for transparent (vacuum bulk) shells under arbitrary dynamical motion; 2) Generalized first law TṠ = AΦ with explicit Φ for physical matter fields; 3) Generalized second law holds when heat flows from hotter to colder regions; 4) Accretion destabilizes throat above geometry- and EOS-dependent critical rate; 5) Stochastic flux induces diffusion and extra entropy production.
AI.conclusion: Thin-shell wormholes admit a robust, physically grounded thermodynamic description; their stability and entropy evolution are highly sensitive to bulk environment and quantum effects—making them potentially observable via gravitational-wave signatures of throat fluctuations or instability.

authors: J. P. A. M. de André
title: Study of Supernova Neutrinos at ESSnuSB
summary: In this paper, we have studied the sensitivity of the ESSnuSB far detector to supernova neutrinos. ESSnuSB is a proposed long-baseline neutrino experiment in Sweden, which will use a 538 kt water Cherenkov detector to probe the leptonic phase $δ_{\rm CP}$ by studying the second oscillation maximum. However, given the very large detector volume, it will have an excellent sensitivity to supernova neutrinos if a supernova explosion occurs during the run-time of ESSnuSB. Motivated by this, we first estimate the expected event rates at the ESSnuSB far detector for three different supernova flux models and then we probe its capability to distinguish these flux models. Additionally, we also investigate the impact of systematic errors and detector efficiency. Our results show that depending on the model of the supernova neutrinos, the expected number of events detected at Earth varies significantly. Our results also show that the ESSnuSB far detector may have excellent potential in distinguishing these flux models depending upon the distance of the supernova explosion, systematic errors and detector efficiency.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates the ESSnuSB far detector’s sensitivity to supernova neutrinos, estimating event rates for three flux models and assessing its capability to distinguish them under varying distances, systematic errors, and detector efficiency.
AI.motivation: The large 538 kt water Cherenkov volume of the proposed ESSnuSB experiment—originally designed for δ_CP measurement via second oscillation maximum—offers exceptional potential for supernova neutrino detection; this work explores that ancillary science capability.
AI.method: Event rate estimation for three supernova neutrino flux models; statistical discrimination analysis between models; evaluation of systematic uncertainties and detector efficiency effects.
AI.result: Expected event counts vary significantly across flux models; ESSnuSB can distinguish among them depending on supernova distance, level of systematics, and detector efficiency.
AI.conclusion: ESSnuSB has strong supplementary potential for supernova neutrino physics, contingent on astrophysical and experimental parameters.

title: Supercool with PPO: Exploring Supercooled Phase Transitions via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Gravitational waves from cosmological first-order phase transitions provide a powerful probe of hidden sectors and beyond the Standard Model physics. However, identifying phenomenologically relevant benchmark points remains computationally challenging, since viable and detectable signals typically occupy only a small fraction of the scanned parameter space. In this work, we introduce a reinforcement learning strategy based on Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to accelerate the search for gravitational wave signals from supercooled phase transitions in a minimal dark $U(1)_x$ sector. We construct a numerical reinforcement learning environment that maps the microscopic model parameters to the corresponding phase transition and gravitational wave observables, using a gauge-independent low-temperature formulation of the effective action. Several reward designs are developed to guide the agent toward parameter regions producing large gravitational wave amplitudes, broad frequency coverage, and detector sensitive benchmark points. We compare the PPO scans with conventional Monte Carlo scans in both narrow and broad windows of the $U(1)_x$ vacuum expectation value. Our results demonstrate that PPO provides an efficient goal-directed search strategy for gravitational wave phenomenology and offers a broadly applicable framework for learning-assisted exploration of high-dimensional scientific parameter spaces.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a reinforcement learning (PPO) method to efficiently search for detectable gravitational wave signals from supercooled first-order phase transitions in a minimal dark U(1)_x model, outperforming conventional Monte Carlo sampling.
AI.motivation: Identifying phenomenologically viable and detectable gravitational wave signals from cosmological first-order phase transitions is computationally expensive due to their sparse distribution in high-dimensional parameter space.
AI.method: A gauge-independent, low-temperature effective action is used to construct a numerical RL environment; Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agents are trained with custom rewards targeting large GW amplitude, broad frequency coverage, and detector sensitivity.
AI.result: PPO achieves significantly higher efficiency than Monte Carlo scans in locating benchmark points—especially in broad parameter windows—while discovering regions with enhanced GW observability.
AI.conclusion: Reinforcement learning, particularly PPO, serves as an efficient, goal-directed strategy for GW phenomenology and provides a generalizable framework for scientific exploration of high-dimensional theory spaces.

title: Charged and rotating near-horizon geometries in five dimensions
summary: We present new charged and rotating near-horizon geometries in five-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell theory in closed analytic form. The solutions can be parametrised by the charge and two independent angular momenta. We also generalise these near-horizon geometries to theories with an additional Chern-Simons term in the action multiplied by an arbitrary coupling constant.
