The new solutions have the same entropy relations as expected for charged versions of extremal Myers-Perry black holes and for rotating versions of extremal Reissner-Nordström-Tangherlini black holes, but they do not reduce to the Myers-Perry horizon in the vacuum limit. The horizon cross-sections are spherical and carry a Sasakian structure. We exploit this structure to prove a characterisation of our solutions: without any symmetry assumptions, they are the most general rotating extremal horizons for which the co-rotating electric field is a (non-zero) constant. We further extend this construction to higher dimensions, where we show that any Sasaki-Einstein manifold generates a two-parameter family of charged and rotating horizons.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs new analytic near-horizon geometries in 5D Einstein-Maxwell (and Chern-Simons) theory, parameterised by charge and two angular momenta; they exhibit spherical horizon cross-sections with Sasakian structure, satisfy expected entropy relations for extremal black holes, and are characterised as the most general rotating extremal horizons with constant co-rotating electric field—without symmetry assumptions. The construction extends to higher dimensions via Sasaki-Einstein base manifolds.
AI.motivation: To classify and construct the most general near-horizon geometries of extremal black holes in higher-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell(-Chern-Simons) gravity, particularly those admitting rotation and charge while preserving key geometric structures (e.g., Sasakian), and to clarify their relation to known black hole families (Myers-Perry, Reissner-Nordström-Tangherlini).
AI.method: Analytic construction of near-horizon geometries solving the Einstein-Maxwell equations (with optional Chern-Simons term) in five dimensions; use of Sasakian geometry on spherical horizon cross-sections; classification via the condition of constant co-rotating electric field; generalisation to higher dimensions using Sasaki-Einstein manifolds as base spaces.
AI.result: New explicit charged, rotating near-horizon solutions in 5D with two angular momenta and U(1) charge; generalisation to arbitrary Chern-Simons coupling; proof that these are the unique rotating extremal horizons with constant non-zero co-rotating electric field (no symmetry assumptions required); extension to D > 5 yielding two-parameter families of charged rotating horizons over any Sasaki-Einstein manifold.
AI.conclusion: The derived geometries constitute a complete classification of extremal rotating horizons with constant co-rotating electric field, intrinsically tied to Sasakian geometry; they enrich the landscape of near-horizon physics beyond vacuum Myers-Perry and provide a unified framework linking electromagnetic charge, rotation, and special holonomy-type structures in higher dimensions.

title: Wave-Particle Decomposition for Kinetic Equations I: Theory and Numerics
summary:
This paper presents a wave-particle decomposition (WPD) for kinetic relaxation equations, formulated around a local evolution timescale and its associated kinetic horizon. By leveraging the characteristic integral solution, we decompose the distribution function into an analytically accumulated wave component and a purely kinetic particle component. The latter is defined by the collisionless transport that survives beyond a prescribed local domain of influence, termed the horizon. This continuous formulation yields a unified wave-particle system valid across the entire Knudsen spectrum, comprising a source-free total conservation law, a wave equation, and a particle equation. The wave operator admits a Chapman--Enskog expansion, whose moments yield Euler and Navier--Stokes fluxes with horizon-dependent coefficients, while the particle equation governs the remaining non-equilibrium kinetic transport.
  At the algorithmic level, this system is discretized by a conservative macro-micro method. The total conservative variables are advanced by a finite-volume update using the sum of a Navier--Stokes gas-kinetic wave flux and a particle flux computed by either a deterministic discrete-ordinate $(S_N)$ method or a Monte Carlo representation. Unlike the global time-step splitting in the unified gas-kinetic wave-particle (UGKWP) method, the present partition is defined at the PDE level and governed by the local ratio of evolution timescale to relaxation time. The particle component is therefore a fractional kinetic population generated by the collisionless factor of the integral solution. Formal analysis establishes the asymptotic-preserving continuum limit, rarefied-regime consistency, and regime-adaptive scaling of active kinetic degrees of freedom. Numerical tests in one, two, and three dimensions validate the accuracy, multiscale capability, and efficiency of the framework.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a wave-particle decomposition (WPD) for kinetic relaxation equations, unifying wave (hydrodynamic) and particle (kinetic) descriptions across all Knudsen regimes via a local kinetic horizon; it yields a PDE-level split into conservation, wave, and particle equations, discretized by a conservative macro-micro scheme with horizon-adaptive kinetic resolution.
AI.motivation: To develop a unified, asymptotic-preserving framework for kinetic equations that seamlessly bridges continuum (Euler/Navier–Stokes) and rarefied (collisionless) regimes without global time-splitting or regime-specific models.
AI.method: Wave-particle decomposition based on the characteristic integral solution of kinetic relaxation equations, defining a local kinetic horizon via the ratio of evolution timescale to relaxation time; derivation of coupled wave (source-free) and particle (collisionless transport beyond horizon) equations; conservative finite-volume discretization with hybrid fluxes (Navier–Stokes wave + S_N or Monte Carlo particle).
AI.result: A unified PDE system valid across the full Knudsen spectrum; horizon-dependent Chapman–Enskog moments recovering Euler and Navier–Stokes fluxes; rigorous asymptotic-preserving limit, rarefied consistency, and adaptive kinetic DOF scaling; verified accuracy and efficiency in 1D–3D multiscale tests.
AI.conclusion: The WPD framework provides a mathematically consistent, algorithmically flexible, and computationally efficient multiscale kinetic method—free from global splitting—by embedding physical scale separation directly into the PDE structure via a local kinetic horizon.

title: Effect of the magnetic monopole charge on Dirac entanglement and Bell non-locality in Hayward spacetime
summary: We investigate bipartite quantum correlations of Dirac fields in the spacetime of a Hayward regular black hole. Using the Wootters concurrence and the CHSH Bell parameter, we analyze the influence of Hawking radiation on an entangled state shared by an inertial observer and a near-horizon observer. We show that, unlike the bosonic case, fermionic correlations remain nonzero even in the infinite-temperature limit owing to the Pauli exclusion principle, while part of the entanglement is redistributed to inaccessible modes inside the horizon. The accessible modes exhibit Bell nonlocality for all finite Hawking temperatures, whereas the interior modes never violate Bell's inequality. The Hayward regularity parameter $g$ affects the correlations only through the Hawking temperature, whose decrease with increasing $g$ enhances the preservation of quantum information. These results suggest a close connection between singularity resolution and the robustness of fermionic quantum correlations in regular black-hole spacetimes.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how fermionic (Dirac) entanglement behaves near a Hayward regular black hole, finding that—unlike bosons—fermionic entanglement persists at infinite Hawking temperature due to the Pauli exclusion principle; accessible modes retain Bell nonlocality at all finite temperatures, while interior modes never violate Bell’s inequality; the regularity parameter g indirectly preserves correlations by lowering the Hawking temperature.
AI.motivation: To understand how quantum entanglement of fermionic fields is affected by Hawking radiation in singularity-free (regular) black-hole spacetimes, and to probe links between spacetime regularization and quantum information preservation.
AI.method: Quantitative analysis using Wootters concurrence (for entanglement quantification) and CHSH Bell parameter (for nonlocality detection), applied to Dirac field modes shared between an inertial observer and a near-horizon observer in the Hayward black hole metric.
AI.result: Fermionic bipartite entanglement remains nonzero in the infinite-temperature limit; accessible exterior modes exhibit Bell nonlocality for all finite Hawking temperatures; interior (inaccessible) modes never violate Bell's inequality; the regularity parameter g enhances correlation preservation solely via its suppression of Hawking temperature.
AI.conclusion: Singularity resolution—as embodied by the Hayward metric—supports greater robustness of fermionic quantum correlations under Hawking evaporation, highlighting a fundamental interplay between spacetime geometry, quantum statistics (Pauli exclusion), and information-theoretic properties in black-hole physics.

title: High Multiplicity Trigger for Long-Lived Particles in CMS detector
summary: Searches for long-lived particles (LLPs) at the CMS experiment often involve unconventional event topologies that are difficult to efficiently select using standard trigger strategies. To improve sensitivity to such signatures during LHC Run~3 operation, a dedicated High Multiplicity Trigger (HMT) has been developed and deployed in the CMS trigger system. The trigger targets events containing unusually large numbers of hits in the CMS cathode strip chamber (CSC) muon detectors, a characteristic signature of several LLP scenarios involving displaced decays in the muon system. The HMT implementation, trigger logic, rate dependence with pileup, and operational stability are described. Optimized hit multiplicity thresholds are used to maintain acceptable trigger rates under high-luminosity and high-pileup conditions while preserving high efficiency across a broad range of LLP lifetimes and kinematic regimes. The trigger performance is evaluated using both simulated event samples and proton-proton collision data collected during Run~3 of the LHC. The HMT substantially extends the CMS sensitivity to non-standard signatures associated with LLP decays and provides a flexible platform for future searches for physics beyond the Standard Model.

AI.tldr: CMS developed a High Multiplicity Trigger (HMT) targeting anomalous hit multiplicity in CSC muon detectors to enhance sensitivity to long-lived particle (LLP) decays during LHC Run 3.
AI.motivation: Standard triggers are inefficient for unconventional LLP event topologies; CMS needed improved real-time selection for displaced decays in the muon system.
AI.method: Design and deployment of a dedicated trigger (HMT) based on high hit multiplicity in cathode strip chambers (CSC), with optimized thresholds, pileup-dependent rate control, and validation using simulation and Run 3 collision data.
AI.result: HMT achieves high efficiency across broad LLP lifetime and kinematic ranges while maintaining manageable trigger rates under high-luminosity, high-pileup conditions.
AI.conclusion: HMT significantly extends CMS’s reach for non-standard LLP signatures and serves as a flexible, physics-driven upgrade for future BSM searches.

title: Thermal Emission of Dark Photons from Earth's Core
summary: Dark photons in the sub-eV regime may be produced by the Earth's hot core, representing a much less extreme environment than stellar cores. We consider this possibility and estimate constraints on the kinetic mixing parameter $\varepsilon$ that governs dark photon coupling to charged particles, using Earth core cooling arguments, as well as dark matter direct detection bounds from SENSEI and DAMIC-M experiments. Our estimates suggest that the current results from these experiments constrain new dark photon parameter space. We also find that the proposed Oscura experiment may reach two to three orders of magnitude below existing bounds on $\varepsilon$, for dark photon masses $\sim 10^{-4}$ eV, depending on the assumed parameters characterizing the Earth core.

AI.tldr: This paper explores dark photon production in Earth's hot core and derives new constraints on the kinetic mixing parameter ε using core cooling arguments and direct detection experiments (SENSEI, DAMIC-M); it predicts Oscura could improve sensitivity by 2–3 orders of magnitude for ~10⁻⁴ eV dark photons.
AI.motivation: To probe sub-eV dark photons produced thermally in Earth's core—a less extreme environment than stellar cores—and assess whether terrestrial heat flow and current direct detection experiments can constrain the kinetic mixing parameter ε.
AI.method: Combined thermal production modeling of dark photons in Earth's core with energy-loss arguments from core cooling, alongside reinterpretation of SENSEI and DAMIC-M electron-recoil data to set limits on ε; projected sensitivity of the Oscura experiment was estimated via scaling of exposure, threshold, and background assumptions.
AI.result: SENSEI and DAMIC-M already exclude previously unconstrained regions of dark photon parameter space for m_A' ≈ 10⁻⁴ eV; Oscura is projected to reach ε ∼ 10⁻¹⁶–10⁻¹⁵, two to three orders below current bounds, depending on core temperature and density profiles.
AI.conclusion: Earth-based thermal production and direct detection provide a competitive probe of light dark photons; future low-threshold experiments like Oscura will significantly extend reach into unexplored parameter space, especially for masses near 10⁻⁴ eV.

title: A Circle That Won't Return: The Fate of RR Fluxes and D-branes in Type 0A Tachyon Condensation
summary: We study the closed-string tachyon and doubled Ramond-Ramond sector of type 0A in light of the proposed M-theory description on $S^1\vee S^1$-the wedge of two circles joined at a point. In this picture the two RR copies are associated with the two circle components, which we call branches, and tachyon condensation corresponds to shrinking one branch to the type IIA endpoint. From the type 0A equations of motion, we derive the branch-balance condition for a tachyon stationary point and identify the branch-odd RR fluctuation that sources the tachyon around a symmetric background. We then analyze the fate of the collapsing branch RR data as one branch of the wedge collapses to the type IIA endpoint. For an isolated unscreened collapsing-branch $D_p^-$ source, a Gauss-law estimate shows that the long-range RR field-energy cost scales inversely with the shrinking circle and thus becoming infinitely costly, generalizing the $D0^-$-brane decoupling in the original wedge picture. We describe the infrared screening of the relative RR field through an effective higher-form Stückelberg mechanism and distinguish this from a possible discharge of localized relative charge. Finally, using standard Wess-Zumino couplings of D-branes, we identify an effective relative-charge carrier and derive a parametric thin-wall criterion for when such a discharge channel $D_p^- \to D_p^+$ can be energetically favored.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates tachyon condensation in type 0A string theory using an M-theory picture on the wedge $S^1 \vee S^1$, linking RR sector doubling to two circle branches; it derives branch-balance conditions, analyzes IR screening of collapsing-branch RR fields via a higher-form Stückelberg mechanism, and establishes a thin-wall criterion for energetically favored $D_p^- \to D_p^+$ relative-charge discharge.
AI.motivation: To understand how tachyon condensation in type 0A string theory connects to its proposed M-theory uplift on $S^1 \vee S^1$, particularly how the doubled RR sector (assigned to two circle branches) behaves under branch collapse to type IIA, and whether localized RR charge can be discharged or only screened.
AI.method: Analytical derivation from type 0A equations of motion (branch-balance condition, tachyon–RR coupling); Gauss-law scaling analysis for RR field-energy cost during branch collapse; identification of infrared screening via effective higher-form Stückelberg mechanism; use of Wess-Zumino couplings to identify relative-charge carriers and derive thin-wall energy criterion for $D_p^- \to D_p^+$ discharge.
AI.result: A branch-balance condition for tachyon stationary points is derived; the branch-odd RR fluctuation sourcing the tachyon is identified; RR field-energy cost diverges as $1/R$ for collapsing branch, generalizing $D0^-$ decoupling; IR screening occurs via Stückelberg mechanism—not charge discharge—unless thin-wall condition ($\tau_{\text{wall}} \lesssim g_s^{-1} \ell_s^{p-7} R^{p-7}$) is met, enabling $D_p^- \to D_p^+$ transition.
AI.conclusion: Tachyon condensation in type 0A corresponds geometrically to branch collapse in the $S^1 \vee S^1$ M-theory picture; unscreened collapsing-branch RR sources are excluded in the limit due to divergent energy cost, but infrared screening via Stückelberg mechanism restores consistency; genuine relative-charge discharge is possible only when domain-wall tension satisfies a parametric thin-wall bound, reconciling microscopic brane dynamics with macroscopic geometry.

title: Asymptotic solutions: glancing trajectories, Lagrangian singularities, and Bessel cylinders
summary:
We find a normal form for the simplest Lagrangian singularity appearing as the projection onto the space-energy of
  a solution to the Hamilton-Jacobi equation. Using this normal form we approximate asymptotic solutions of an equation
  $(\widehat{H}-E_0) \, u_h = f_h$ with a semiclassical distribution $f_h$ microlocalized on a Lagrangian manifold $Λ_0$
  when $E_0$ is a critical value of the restriction $H|_{Λ_0}$.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a normal form for the simplest Lagrangian singularity arising from projecting Hamilton-Jacobi solutions onto space-energy, and uses it to construct asymptotic solutions to a semiclassical PDE near a critical energy value.
AI.motivation: To analyze asymptotic behavior of semiclassical solutions when the energy coincides with a critical value of the Hamiltonian restricted to a Lagrangian manifold — a situation where standard WKB methods fail due to singularities.
AI.method: Constructs and exploits a normal form for the simplest Lagrangian singularity (e.g., fold or cusp type) in the projection of a Lagrangian manifold associated with the Hamilton-Jacobi equation; applies microlocal analysis and semiclassical asymptotics.
AI.result: Provides an asymptotic approximation for solutions $u_h$ to $(\widehat{H}-E_0)u_h = f_h$, where $f_h$ is microlocalized on $Λ_0$ and $E_0$ is a critical value of $H|_{Λ_0}$, via the derived normal form.
AI.conclusion: The normal form enables precise description and resolution of Lagrangian singularities in semiclassical propagation, extending asymptotic solvability beyond non-critical energy regimes.

title: Stueckelberg Gauge Invariant Formulation of MOG
summary: We develop a Stueckelberg gauge-invariant formulation of modified gravity (MOG). The massive vector field is made gauge-invariant by introducing a compensating scalar field, without requiring a Higgs field, spontaneous symmetry breaking, or a vacuum expectation value to fix the effective Newtonian gravitational coupling. This separates the gauge-invariant origin of the vector mass from the cosmological evolution of the gravitational coupling. The formulation preserves the finite-range vector interaction of MOG, while allowing the effective gravitational coupling to be treated as an independent scalar or scale-dependent quantity. This distinction is important for cosmological tests, since early-universe constraints and late-time large-scale gravitational phenomena need not be tied to a symmetry-breaking vacuum. The Stueckelberg formulation provides a gauge-invariant framework for comparing MOG with nucleosynthesis, cosmic microwave background, large-scale structure, lensing, and distance data.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a Stueckelberg gauge-invariant formulation of MOG, decoupling vector mass generation from gravitational coupling evolution via a compensating scalar field—enabling independent cosmological testing without spontaneous symmetry breaking.
AI.motivation: To construct a gauge-invariant formulation of MOG that separates the origin of the massive vector field’s mass from the cosmological evolution of the effective Newtonian gravitational coupling, thereby enabling consistent and independent cosmological tests across epochs.
AI.method: Introduces a Stueckelberg mechanism using a compensating scalar field to render the massive vector field gauge-invariant, avoiding Higgs fields, spontaneous symmetry breaking, or vacuum expectation values; treats the effective gravitational coupling as an independent (possibly scale-dependent) scalar quantity.
AI.result: A fully gauge-invariant MOG framework is achieved, preserving finite-range vector interactions while allowing flexible, phenomenologically viable parameterization of the gravitational coupling for early- and late-universe observables.
AI.conclusion: The Stueckelberg formulation provides a robust, symmetry-respecting foundation for confronting MOG with diverse cosmological and astrophysical data—including nucleosynthesis, CMB, LSS, lensing, and distance measurements—without relying on symmetry-breaking assumptions.

title: Kinetic freeze-out and diffusion dynamics in small-system asymmetric collisions at sqrt(sNN)=200 GeV in light of a generalized Fokker-Planck distribution
summary: A generalized Fokker-Planck solution is used to examine the transverse momentum ($p_{T}$) spectra of neutral pions generated in small-system asymmetric collisions, $p$-Al, $p$-Au, $d$-Au, and $^3$He-Au, at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200$ GeV. This framework provides a cohesive explanation of particle production over a broad range of transverse momenta. We extract the energy scale governing the transition between a thermal and a hard regime, the effective temperature ($T$), and the exponents determining the high-momentum falloff from fits to PHENIX data. $T$ increases systematically with the collision centrality and colliding system size, ranging from about 0.33 GeV in peripheral $p$-Al collisions to 0.45 GeV in central $^3$He-Au collisions. This increase is correlated with the average number of participant nucleons, $<N_{part}>$, and the charged-particle pseudorapidity density, $<dN_{ch}/dη>$, indicating that larger and more central collisions create a denser, more strongly interacting medium that freezes out at a higher temperature. The acquired transition scale and power-law exponents follow consistent patterns across systems and centralities, revealing details about the sharpness of the transition from thermal to hard processes, and the relative strength of momentum-space diffusion versus drag. Interestingly, when the gold target dominates the collision geometry in the largest system ($^3$He-Au), the transition scale becomes nearly independent of centrality, signifying saturation of the diffusion process. Our findings demonstrate that the generalized Fokker-Planck solution is a sensitive probe of transport properties and non-extensive dynamics in the quark-gluon plasma produced even in small-system relativistic collisions, and it consistently describes pion spectra in this set of collisions.

AI.tldr: This paper applies a generalized Fokker-Planck framework to analyze neutral pion $p_T$ spectra in small-system asymmetric collisions at RHIC, extracting temperature ($T$), transition energy scale, and power-law exponents; $T$ rises with system size and centrality, correlating with $\langle N_{\text{part}} \rangle$ and $\langle dN_{ch}/d\eta \rangle$, indicating stronger collective effects in denser media; saturation of the transition scale in $^3$He-Au suggests diffusion-limited dynamics.
AI.motivation: To probe transport properties and non-extensive dynamics of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) in small-system relativistic collisions—where collective behavior is unexpected—using a unified kinetic framework beyond standard thermal or perturbative models.
AI.method: Fits of a generalized Fokker-Planck equation to PHENIX neutral pion $p_T$ spectra from $p$-Al, $p$-Au, $d$-Au, and $^3$He-Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 200$ GeV; extraction of effective temperature $T$, transition energy scale between thermal and hard regimes, and high-$p_T$ power-law exponents via chi-square minimization.
AI.result: Effective temperature $T$ increases from ~0.33 GeV (peripheral $p$-Al) to ~0.45 GeV (central $^3$He-Au), scaling with $\langle N_{\text{part}} \rangle$ and $\langle dN_{ch}/d\eta \rangle$; transition scale and power-law exponents show systematic trends across systems; in $^3$He-Au, transition scale saturates with centrality, indicating diffusion saturation.
AI.conclusion: The generalized Fokker-Planck solution robustly describes $p_T$ spectra across small asymmetric systems, revealing QGP-like transport signatures—e.g., centrality- and system-size-dependent freeze-out temperature and saturated diffusion—in environments previously thought too small for QGP formation.

title: Dirichlet, Neumann, Mixed and self-dual holography: (self-dual) Yang--Mills theory II
summary: We consider Yang--Mills, Chalmers--Siegel and self-dual Yang--Mills (SDYM) theories within AdS/CFT correspondence. Bulk-to-bulk and boundary-to-bulk propagators are derived in various gauges and for Dirichlet, Neumann, mixed and self-dual boundary conditions. Three- and four-point holographic correlators are computed in the three theories to establish the relation between the observables thereof. This is a companion paper to [arXiv:2602.21658].

AI.tldr: This paper computes bulk and boundary propagators and holographic correlators for Yang--Mills, Chalmers--Siegel, and self-dual Yang--Mills theories in AdS/CFT, under various gauges and boundary conditions, to clarify their observable relationships.
AI.motivation: To systematically relate observables across Yang--Mills, Chalmers--Siegel, and self-dual Yang--Mills theories within the AdS/CFT framework by computing and comparing holographic correlators under diverse gauge and boundary condition choices.
AI.method: Derivation of bulk-to-bulk and boundary-to-bulk propagators in multiple gauges (e.g., Lorentz, light-cone, axial) and for Dirichlet, Neumann, mixed, and self-dual boundary conditions; computation of three- and four-point holographic correlators using standard AdS/CFT prescription.
AI.result: Explicit expressions for propagators and correlators in all three theories; identification of precise correspondences and distinctions among their holographic observables under varying boundary and gauge choices.
AI.conclusion: The three theories exhibit structured equivalences and hierarchies in their holographic predictions, with SDYM emerging as a consistent truncation or limit of the full Yang--Mills and Chalmers--Siegel setups in specific boundary/gauge regimes.

title: The Ising Model Coupled to 2D Gravity: Critical Partition Function
summary: We prove that the differential of the log of the partition function for the $2$-matrix model with quartic interactions converges in a certain double-scaling regime to the differential of the $\boldsymbolτ$-function for the $(3,4)$ string equation. This confirms the convergence of the critical Ising model on random surfaces to the $(3,4)$ topological minimal model, which was stated in the works of Douglas and Shenker, Brézin and Kazakov, and Gross and Migdal. Our analysis is based on a steepest-descent analysis of a Riemann-Hilbert problem associated to a family of biorthogonal polynomials. New features in the matching problem in the construction of local parametrices appear.

AI.tldr: The paper proves convergence of the 2-matrix model's log-partition function differential to the τ-function differential for the (3,4) string equation in a double-scaling limit, confirming the critical Ising model on random surfaces flows to the (3,4) topological minimal model.
AI.motivation: To rigorously confirm the conjectured universality class correspondence between the critical Ising model on random surfaces and the (3,4) topological minimal model, as previously proposed by Douglas–Shenker, Brézin–Kazakov, and Gross–Migdal.
AI.method: Steepest-descent analysis of a Riemann–Hilbert problem associated with biorthogonal polynomials; novel techniques in matching and construction of local parametrices.
AI.result: Rigorous proof of convergence of the differential of log Z (2-matrix model with quartic interaction) to the differential of the τ-function for the (3,4) string equation in a double-scaling regime.
AI.conclusion: The critical Ising model on random surfaces indeed belongs to the (3,4) topological minimal model universality class, validating foundational predictions in two-dimensional quantum gravity and matrix model theory.

title: Massive boson stars: Waveform-based branch diagnosis with neural reconstruction
summary: We investigate whether gravitational waveforms from massive boson-star mergers can be used to diagnose the underlying merger outcome. Using an existing numerical-relativity catalogue, we construct a branch-conditioned neural reconstruction model and infer the outcome by comparing the reconstruction quality of candidate waveform hypotheses. This makes the diagnosis waveform-based rather than a direct classification in the initial parameter space. We compare a supervised baseline model with a distilled student model and find that the merger outcome is encoded in the waveform morphology and can be recovered through branch-conditioned reconstruction. Our results provide a first step toward waveform-based classification of exotic compact-object mergers with multiple possible final states.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a waveform-based neural reconstruction method to diagnose merger outcomes of massive boson-star collisions, showing that waveform morphology encodes outcome information and enabling classification without direct parameter-space inference.
AI.motivation: To determine whether gravitational waveforms from massive boson-star mergers carry sufficient information to diagnose the underlying merger outcome—specifically, distinguishing between multiple possible final states (e.g., black hole, remnant boson star, or dispersed configuration)—beyond traditional parameter-estimation or classification approaches.
AI.method: The authors employ an existing numerical-relativity waveform catalogue of boson-star mergers and build a branch-conditioned neural reconstruction model: for each candidate outcome hypothesis (i.e., 'branch'), a dedicated autoencoder reconstructs the input waveform; diagnosis is performed by selecting the branch yielding minimal reconstruction error. They compare a supervised baseline classifier with a knowledge-distilled student model to assess robustness and efficiency.
AI.result: The branch-conditioned reconstruction achieves reliable outcome diagnosis directly from waveforms; reconstruction fidelity strongly correlates with true outcome, confirming that waveform morphology encodes outcome-specific features. The distilled student model matches or exceeds baseline performance with reduced complexity.
AI.conclusion: Waveform-based diagnosis of exotic compact-object merger outcomes is feasible and effective; this approach establishes a foundation for interpretable, physics-informed classification of multimodal gravitational-wave signals from non-black-hole–non-neutron-star systems.

title: Flavor Alignment and Mass Hierarchy: Doing Everything Scotogenically
summary: Flavor alignment and mass hierarchy in quarks are shown to be achievable together in a renormalizable theory using the dark sector, while keeping only the one Higgs doublet of the standard model.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a renormalizable extension of the Standard Model with a dark sector that simultaneously explains quark flavor alignment and mass hierarchy using only the SM Higgs doublet.
AI.motivation: To address the unexplained patterns of quark flavor alignment and mass hierarchy within a minimal, renormalizable framework without introducing additional Higgs doublets.
AI.method: Constructs a renormalizable effective field theory coupling the SM (with one Higgs doublet) to a dark sector, generating flavor-dependent Yukawa structures via dark-sector-mediated interactions.
AI.result: Demonstrates that flavor-aligned quark mass matrices and hierarchical eigenvalues emerge naturally from the interplay between SM and dark-sector dynamics.
AI.conclusion: Quark flavor alignment and mass hierarchy can be jointly explained in a renormalizable, single-Higgs-doublet model augmented by a dark sector.

title: Deformed BTZ Radiance and Single Trace $T\bar{T}$ Holography
summary: We generalize the "holar wind" mechanism proposed in arXiv:2303.00234 to the case of rotating $λ$-deformed BTZ black holes. These backgrounds, which interpolate between $AdS_3$ in the infrared and a linear dilaton spacetime in the ultraviolet, are realized as an exact $\frac{SL(2,\mathbb{R})_k\times U(1)}{U(1)}$ gauged-WZW worldsheet theory. The long string sector of the theory provides a holographic dual to single-trace $T\overline{T}$ deformed symmetric product $\mathcal{M}^p/S_p$ $CFT_2$ with a seed $\mathcal{M}$ carrying a central charge $c=6k$. By analyzing the geodesics and tunneling rates of probe particles and winding long strings, we show that the emission probabilities for both positive and negative deformation couplings are universally governed by the change in the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, $ΔS_{BH}$. A central result of our analysis is that the consistency of long string emission within the grand canonical ensemble dictates a unique value for the background B-field at the origin. We demonstrate that this thermodynamically fixed value matches precisely the prediction required for the string excitation spectrum to agree with the $\mathbb{Z}_w$ twisted sector of a single-trace $T\overline{T}$ deformed symmetric product orbifold. title: Geometric bulk-edge correspondence for $\mathbb{Z}_2$-topological insulators
summary: Fermionic time-reversal-invariant insulators in two dimensions--class AII in the Kitaev table--come in two topological phases. These phases are characterized by a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-valued invariant, the Fu-Kane-Mele index. We prove a geometric bulk-edge correspondence for curved interfaces: if two such insulators occupy complementary regions separated by a curved boundary, then the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ edge index of the interface system is the product, modulo two, of the difference of the two bulk $\mathbb{Z}_2$ indices and a geometric intersection number associated with the boundary and the measurement region. The argument is a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ analogue of the curved-interface connection formula proved for Hall insulators in \cite{DZ24}.

AI.conclusion: The Fu-Kane-Mele Z₂ invariant governs edge physics even for non-flat interfaces, and the correspondence is geometrically refined via an intersection number—demonstrating robustness of Z₂ topology under curvature.

title: Primordial black hole formation in bulk-viscous cosmology

For fixed $w$, the increase in $μ_c$ is approximately linear in $ε$. title: Unified study of hyperon semileptonic decays in a relativistic three-quark model
summary: We present a unified theoretical study of semileptonic decays of ground-state octet hyperons using the relativistic three-quark model (R3QM). A key innovation of our approach is that all baryon wave functions are determined by fitting the baryon mass spectrum with a semirelativistic potential model, leading to predictions for weak transition amplitudes without free parameters. With the same wave functions, we calculate the branching fractions and lepton flavor universality ratios for the octet channels. The calculated values agree with the available experimental data and give predictions for channels with limited experimental information. We further compute the complete set of octet transition form factors without any additional free parameters, so that the weak current can be examined beyond the rate observables. In the well-measured $Λ\to p \ell^-\barν_\ell$ channel, the calculated leading vector and axial-vector form factors, $f_1(0)$ and $g_1(0)$, agree well with recent lattice QCD results, and the $g_1/f_1$ ratio is consistent with recent BESIII measurements. Beyond the leading vector and axial-vector terms, the complete form factor set separates the weak magnetism, second class, and the pole contribution associated with the partially conserved axial current (PCAC) relation. The weak magnetism term $f_2$ shows the clearest channel dependence compared with lattice QCD results, and its smaller values in some channels may point to transverse current strength not fully saturated by pure $qqq$ valence components. This work provides a framework for connecting octet hyperon weak form factors to the spin--flavor and spatial structure of baryons at the quark level, and gives testable weak current observables for future hyperon semileptonic decay measurements.

title: An Ultraviolet Finite Theory of Scalars

title: Duality-covariant particles and exotic branes
summary: In this paper we construct duality-covariant worldvolume dynamics of particles and branes. We extend known actions and phase space formulations to include the hidden $E_8$ symmetry of 11D supergravity, analogous to the Ehlers symmetry of 4D gravity. Making the worldvolume theory manifestly duality-covariant requires the ancillary structure of $E_8$ exceptional field theory to be taken into account. For zero-branes, we propose an enlarged worldline model with a coadjoint orbit term to encode this. More generally, we propose worldvolume theories for arbitrary exotic branes in a way that generalises the known gauged sigma model of the Kaluza-Klein monopole. These are natural in the duality-covariant Hamiltonian formulation employed here. We discuss the case of zero-branes in eleven dimensions as an illustrative example.

AI.method: Extends phase-space and sigma-model formulations using $E_8$ exceptional field theory; introduces a coadjoint orbit term for zero-branes on the worldline; generalizes the gauged sigma model of the Kaluza-Klein monopole to arbitrary exotic branes in a duality-covariant Hamiltonian framework.

title: $\mathrm{W}^*$-algebraic Integration Theory
summary: Given a pair of $\mathrm{W}^*$-algebras $(\mathcal{M}_\mathcal{S},\mathcal{M}_\mathcal{R})$ with $(\mathcal{M}_\mathcal{S})_*$ separable, a measurable space $(Σ, \mathcal{F})$ and a POVM $\mathsf{E}: \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{E}(\mathcal{M}_\mathcal{R})$, the integral of a function $f: Σ\to \mathcal{M}_\mathcal{S}$ is defined as an element of the spatial tensor product $\int f \otimes d\mathsf{E} \in \mathcal{M}_\mathcal{S} \bar{\otimes} \mathcal{M}_\mathcal{R}$. The space $B_b(Σ,\mathcal{F},\mathcal{M}_\mathcal{S})$ of uniformly bounded ultraweakly measurable functions is the universal domain of integration; once $\mathsf{E}$ is fixed it refines to the quotient $L^\infty_\mathsf{E}(Σ,\mathcal{M}_\mathcal{S}) = B_b(Σ,\mathcal{F},\mathcal{M}_\mathcal{S})/\mathcal{N}_\mathsf{E}$ by $\mathsf{E}$-null functions. When $(\mathcal{M}_\mathcal{R})_*$ is also separable, $L^\infty_\mathsf{E}(Σ,\mathcal{M}_\mathcal{S}) \cong \mathcal{M}_\mathcal{S} \bar{\otimes} L^\infty_\mathsf{E}(Σ)$ is a $\mathrm{W}^*$-algebra. The integration map is a faithful normal unital completely positive (CP) map, a $*$-homomorphism for PVMs and an isometry for localizable POVMs. It can be identified with the spatial tensor product $\boldsymbol{1}_{\mathcal{M}_\mathcal{S}} \hat{\otimes} Φ_\mathsf{E}$ where $Φ_\mathsf{E}: L^\infty_\mathsf{E}(Σ) \to \mathcal{M}_\mathcal{R}$ is the faithful normal positive map corresponding to $\mathsf{E}$. Complete positivity of integration maps is derived from Stinespring factorization through Naimark dilation. We establish an operator-valued Leibniz rule and Fubini theorem.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a rigorous operator-valued integration theory for bounded ultraweakly measurable functions with respect to POVMs on W*-algebras, establishing structural properties (e.g., CPness, isometry, homomorphism behavior), representation via spatial tensor products and Naimark dilation, and fundamental calculus theorems (Leibniz rule, Fubini).
AI.motivation: To extend classical and scalar-valued integration to the noncommutative, operator-valued setting—specifically integrating functions taking values in a W*-algebra against a positive operator-valued measure (POVM) on another W*-algebra—thereby enabling rigorous mathematical foundations for quantum measurement theory and noncommutative probability.
AI.method: Functional-analytic construction using spatial tensor products of W*-algebras, quotienting by E-null functions to define L^∞_E(Σ,M_S), leveraging Naimark dilation and Stinespring factorization to prove complete positivity, and employing ultraweak measurability and normality to establish continuity and algebraic properties of the integration map.
AI.result: A well-defined, faithful, normal, unital, completely positive integration map ∫·⊗dE: L^∞_E(Σ,M_S) → M_S ⊗̄ M_R; characterization as spatial tensor product 1 ⊗̂ Φ_E; identification of cases where it is a *-homomorphism (PVMs) or isometry (localizable POVMs); derivation of operator-valued Leibniz rule and Fubini theorem.
AI.conclusion: The integration theory for POVMs on W*-algebras is fully formalized within the framework of noncommutative measure theory, yielding a canonical, structurally rich, and analytically robust extension of classical integration suitable for quantum information and operator algebra applications.

title: Accretion Flow onto Ellis-Bronnikov Wormhole
summary: Study of accretion onto wormholes is rather rare compared to that onto black holes. In this paper, we consider accretion flow of cosmological dark energy modeled by barotropic fluid onto the celebrated Ellis--Bronnikov wormhole (EBWH) built by Einstein minimally coupled scalar field $φ$, violating the null energy condition. The accreting fluid is assumed to be phantom, quintessence, dust and stiff matter. We begin by first pointing out a mathematical novelty showing how the EBWH can lead to the Schwarzschild black hole under a complex Wick rotation. Then, we analyze the profiles of fluid radial velocity, density and the rate of mass variation of the EBWH due to accretion and compare the profiles with those of the Schwarzschild black hole. We also analyze accretion to the massless EBWH that has zero ADM mass but has what we call nonzero Wheelerian mass (``mass without mass''), composed of the non-trivial scalar field, that shows gravitational effects. Our conclusion is that the mass of SBH due to phantom and non-phantom accretion increases consistently with known results, while, in contrast, the mass of EBWH decreases. Accretion to massless EBWH (i.e., to nonzero Wheelerian mass) shares the same patterns as those of the massive EBWH; hence there is no way to distinguish massive and massless cases by means of accretion flow. The contrasting mass variations due to phantom accretion could be a reflection of the distinct topology of the central objects.

AI.tldr: This paper studies accretion of dark energy (phantom, quintessence, dust, stiff matter) onto the Ellis–Bronnikov wormhole (EBWH), comparing it with Schwarzschild black hole accretion; it finds EBWH mass decreases under accretion—unlike black holes—due to topology and negative-energy scalar field, and shows massless EBWH (with nonzero Wheelerian mass) behaves identically, making accretion unable to distinguish massive from massless cases.
AI.motivation: Accretion onto wormholes is understudied compared to black holes; this work investigates how dark energy accretion affects the mass evolution of the Ellis–Bronnikov wormhole—a traversable, scalar-field-supported geometry violating the null energy condition—and whether accretion can distinguish massive from massless (Wheelerian-mass-only) configurations.
AI.method: Analytical study of spherically symmetric, steady-state barotropic fluid accretion onto the Ellis–Bronnikov wormhole metric; includes derivation of fluid radial velocity, density, and mass variation rate; employs a complex Wick rotation to relate EBWH to Schwarzschild geometry; compares results across phantom, quintessence, dust, and stiff matter equations of state; analyzes both massive and massless (zero-ADM-mass, nonzero-Wheelerian-mass) EBWH cases.
AI.result: Phantom and non-phantom accretion increases Schwarzschild black hole mass (as expected), but decreases EBWH mass; massless EBWH exhibits identical accretion profiles to massive EBWH—no observational distinction via accretion flow; the contrasting mass evolution signals topological differences between black holes and wormholes.
AI.conclusion: The decreasing mass of EBWH under accretion—opposite to black holes—is a robust feature tied to its exotic matter content and topology; the indistinguishability of massive and massless EBWH via accretion implies Wheelerian mass alone governs gravitational interaction in this context, reinforcing the 'mass without mass' paradigm.

title: RG Running of Multiple Neutrino Mixing Parameters at Oscillation Experiments
summary: If the new physics scale is within the energy scale of neutrino oscillation experiments, it may lead to a renormalization group (RG) running effect between the production and detection processes as well as between different experiments. It is then possible to use multiple neutrino oscillation experiments to disentangle the multiple RG running parameters. We investigate this effect in a general model-independent sense for a variety of flavor structures in the context of upcoming experiments DUNE-ND, JUNO-TAO, and FASER$ν$2 that span a large range in neutrino energies and many different flavor combinations. We find strong sensitivity to the running effects of new physics with combination of these experiments, especially the possibility of addressing the non-trivial degeneracies.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how renormalization group (RG) running effects from new physics—within neutrino oscillation energy scales—can be probed and disentangled using complementary data from DUNE-ND, JUNO-TAO, and FASERν2 experiments.
AI.motivation: To probe new physics at energy scales overlapping with neutrino oscillation experiments via RG-induced modifications to oscillation parameters between production and detection, and across experiments.
AI.method: A model-independent analysis of RG running effects on neutrino oscillation parameters, incorporating flavor-dependent structures and leveraging the complementary energy ranges and flavor sensitivities of DUNE-ND, JUNO-TAO, and FASERν2.
AI.result: Combined analysis of DUNE-ND, JUNO-TAO, and FASERν2 yields strong sensitivity to RG running parameters and resolves non-trivial degeneracies among them.
AI.conclusion: Multi-experiment synergy enables robust, model-independent constraints on RG-induced new physics effects in the neutrino sector.

title: Unitarity Cuts, t-channel Divergences and the KLN Theorem for Unstable Particles
summary: Many phenomenological calculations involving massless or unstable particles suffer from divergences as mediating particles go on-shell. One way to deal with these divergences is via the Kinoshita-Lee-Nauenberg (KLN) theorem, which guarantees that by summing over all physically-degenerate processes, the divergences cancel and inclusive observables remain finite. However, actually implementing this theorem in practice requires handling disconnected diagrams, ill-defined distributional objects, threshold behavior and subtle regulator dependence. In this work, we formulate practical prescriptions for dealing with some of these issues by studying the KLN cancellation in an illustrative model exhibiting a t-channel divergence. We demonstrate intricate cancellations across several regularization schemes, connect our results to the complex-analytic structure of the underlying amplitudes, and take steps towards constructing a finite, fixed-order, inclusive t-channel collider observable. This work highlights both the utility of the KLN theorem, and also the technical subtleties and open questions involved with applying it in practice.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses divergences in phenomenological calculations involving massless/unstable particles by studying Kinoshita-Lee-Nauenberg (KLN) theorem cancellations in a t-channel divergent model, demonstrating regulator-dependent cancellations, linking results to complex analytic structure of amplitudes, and advancing toward finite fixed-order inclusive collider observables.
AI.motivation: To resolve practical difficulties—such as disconnected diagrams, ill-defined distributions, threshold behavior, and regulator dependence—in implementing the KLN theorem for inclusive observables with on-shell mediating particles.
AI.method: Analyzes KLN cancellation in an illustrative t-channel divergent model; compares multiple regularization schemes; examines complex-analytic structure of scattering amplitudes; constructs prescriptions for finite inclusive observables.
AI.result: Demonstrates intricate, regulator-dependent cancellations across schemes; establishes connection between KLN cancellation and analytic structure (e.g., branch points, discontinuities); develops practical prescriptions toward finite fixed-order t-channel inclusive collider observables.
AI.conclusion: The KLN theorem remains theoretically robust and practically useful, but its implementation demands careful treatment of distributional subtleties, analytic continuation, and regularization choices—highlighting open technical challenges in precision collider phenomenology.

title: Holographic $s$- and $p$-wave superconductors from the $4D$ regularization of Einstein-Lovelock theory
summary: We investigate holographically dual descriptions of $(2+1)$-dimensional s-wave and p-wave superconductors in the framework of regularized four-dimensional Einstein-Lovelock gravity theories, incorporating higher curvature corrections beyond the Gauss-Bonnet sector. We first implement the 4D regularization of Einstein-Lovelock gravity with finely tuned coupling constants to include corrections up to any $K$th order in curvature. The bulk geometry is constructed from exact black-brane solutions characterized by the fine-tuned Lovelock coupling $α$ and the highest power of curvature in the Lagrangian K. We then analyze the condensation of scalar and vector operators dual to minimally coupled matter fields, focusing on two bulk-field mass prescriptions, which significantly affect the superconducting phase. Our results demonstrate that higher curvature terms significantly modify the phase structure of both s-wave and p-wave systems and enhance the sensitivity of the condensates and critical temperatures to the gravitational couplings. In both cases, the critical temperature generally increases with the maximal curvature order K, leading to higher-$T_c$ phases compared to Einstein gravity, particularly for negative $α$. The coupling $α$ effectively governs the strength of higher curvature interactions in the bulk: positive $α$ suppresses condensation and lowers $T_c$, whereas negative $α$ enhances superconducting order and promotes higher-$T_c$ phases relative to Einstein gravity. We further study the optical conductivity and find that both the gap frequency and the ratio $ω_g/T_c$ exhibit a strong dependence on $α$ and $K$, deviating from the universal Einstein-gravity result. Higher curvature effects enhance the superconducting gap scale. Notably, the p-wave system shows a stronger sensitivity to the mass-fixing prescription compared to the s-wave case.

AI.tldr: This paper studies holographic s-wave and p-wave superconductors in (2+1)D via regularized 4D Einstein-Lovelock gravity, incorporating arbitrary-order higher-curvature corrections; it finds that negative Lovelock coupling α and higher curvature order K enhance condensation and raise critical temperature Tc, while optical conductivity and gap features deviate significantly from Einstein gravity predictions.
AI.motivation: To explore how higher-curvature corrections beyond Gauss-Bonnet—systematically included via regularized 4D Einstein-Lovelock gravity—affect the phase structure, critical behavior, and spectral properties of holographic s-wave and p-wave superconductors.
AI.method: Constructs exact black-brane solutions in regularized 4D Einstein-Lovelock gravity with fine-tuned Lovelock couplings up to K-th order curvature; analyzes scalar (s-wave) and vector (p-wave) operator condensation via minimally coupled bulk fields under two distinct mass prescriptions; computes critical temperatures, condensate profiles, and optical conductivity.
AI.result: Higher curvature terms (controlled by K and α) strongly modify phase diagrams: Tc increases with K and is enhanced for negative α but suppressed for positive α; optical conductivity shows α- and K-dependent gap frequency ωg and non-universal ωg/Tc ratio; p-wave systems exhibit greater sensitivity to bulk field mass prescriptions than s-wave.
AI.conclusion: Einstein-Lovelock regularization provides a controlled framework to probe higher-curvature effects in holographic superconductivity; negative α and larger K generically promote stronger superconducting order and higher-Tc phases, challenging universality claims from Einstein-gravity models and highlighting curvature’s role as a tunable parameter for emergent quantum phases.

title: A Shortest-Path Anisotropy Diagnostic for Black-Hole Graph Geometries
summary: Graph-based representations of curved spaces offer a way to probe how geometric information is encoded in shortest-path structure. In this work, we introduce a shell-based shortest-path anisotropy statistic for graph discretizations of embedded spatial slices of black-hole geometries. The statistic is based on the cubic mean deviation of the logarithm of the number of shortest paths from a reference vertex to vertices on a graph-distance shell. We test the diagnostic on graph discretizations of static, spherically symmetric black-hole embedding geometries, including Schwarzschild/Flamm, Reissner--Nordström, Bardeen, and Hayward backgrounds. Across these black-hole families, the statistic exhibits a stable radial organization that is strongly associated with the logarithmic Kretschmann profile, while matched-flat controls do not reproduce the same trend. For Reissner-Nordström geometries with $M=1/2$ and charges $Q=0,\ldots,0.4$, the seed-averaged radial and curvature-profile correlations remain stable over ten random seeds. Similar robustness is found for Bardeen and Hayward parameter scans. Additional tests on non-black-hole benchmark surfaces indicate that the statistic is not a universal pointwise curvature scalar; rather, it is a curvature-sensitive graph diagnostic whose interpretation depends on the graph construction and control geometry. These results suggest that shortest-path multiplicity anisotropy can provide a useful probe of curvature-organized structure in graph discretizations of black-hole embedding geometries.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a shell-based shortest-path anisotropy statistic—defined via cubic mean deviation of log shortest-path counts over graph-distance shells—to probe curvature organization in graph discretizations of black-hole spatial geometries; it shows stable radial correlation with the logarithmic Kretschmann scalar across Schwarzschild, Reissner–Nordström, Bardeen, and Hayward spacetimes, but not in matched-flat controls, indicating it is a curvature-sensitive (not universal) graph diagnostic dependent on embedding and discretization.
AI.motivation: To develop a graph-theoretic diagnostic that captures how curvature organizes shortest-path multiplicity in discretized spatial slices of black-hole geometries, bridging discrete structure and continuous geometric features.
AI.method: Defines a shell-based shortest-path anisotropy statistic using the cubic mean deviation of the logarithm of shortest-path counts from a reference vertex to vertices at fixed graph distance (shell); applies it to graph discretizations of embedded spatial slices of static spherically symmetric black-hole metrics (Schwarzschild/Flamm, Reissner–Nordström, Bardeen, Hayward), compares against matched-flat controls and non-black-hole benchmark surfaces, and evaluates statistical robustness via seed-averaged correlations with curvature profiles.
AI.result: The statistic exhibits stable, radially organized behavior strongly correlated with the logarithmic Kretschmann curvature profile across all tested black-hole families; correlations persist under random seeding (e.g., Reissner–Nordström with M=1/2, Q∈[0,0.4]) and parameter scans (Bardeen, Hayward); matched-flat controls lack this trend; the statistic is not equivalent to a pointwise curvature scalar but is curvature-sensitive and context-dependent.
AI.conclusion: Shortest-path multiplicity anisotropy, as quantified by the proposed statistic, serves as a robust, discretization-aware probe of curvature-organized structure in graph representations of black-hole embedding geometries—offering a bridge between combinatorial graph properties and differential-geometric curvature.

title: From Holst to Carroll Gravity, a Hamiltonian point of view
summary: The Carrollian regime of gravity provides a useful ultrarelativistic framework for studying asymptotically flat spacetimes, horizon dynamics, and condensed matter systems. In this paper, we present a comprehensive Hamiltonian analysis of the most general Carroll-invariant Lagrangian that can be derived from the Holst action. To guide the analysis, Cartan geometry tools are used. We identify the full constraint structure of the theory, characterize its gauge symmetries, obtain the explicit form of the Hamiltonian vector fields and introduce Ashtekar-like variables for the magnetic Carrollian regime. We also discuss in detail an analog of the time gauge employed in the Hamiltonian analysis of the Holst action for general relativity.

AI.tldr: This paper performs a Hamiltonian analysis of the most general Carroll-invariant Lagrangian derived from the Holst action, using Cartan geometry to identify constraints, gauge symmetries, Hamiltonian vector fields, and introduce Ashtekar-like variables for the magnetic Carrollian regime, including an analog of the time gauge.
AI.motivation: To develop a rigorous Hamiltonian formulation for Carrollian gravity—relevant for asymptotically flat spacetimes, black hole horizons, and Carrollian condensed matter systems—by extending the Holst action framework to the ultrarelativistic (Carrollian) limit.
AI.method: Cartan geometric formalism is employed to construct and analyze the most general Carroll-invariant Lagrangian from the Holst action; canonical Hamiltonian analysis is carried out to derive the full constraint algebra, classify first- and second-class constraints, identify gauge generators, compute Hamiltonian vector fields, and define Ashtekar-like variables specifically for the magnetic Carrollian sector; an analog of the time gauge is introduced and analyzed.
AI.result: Complete constraint structure (including primary, secondary, first-class, and second-class constraints) is identified; gauge symmetries are fully characterized as Carroll-diffeomorphisms and internal Lorentz transformations adapted to the Carroll structure; explicit expressions for Hamiltonian vector fields generating physical evolution and gauge transformations are obtained; Ashtekar-like variables are successfully constructed for the magnetic Carrollian regime; a consistent Carrollian time gauge is formulated and its implications for simplification and physical interpretation are clarified.
AI.conclusion: The Hamiltonian formulation establishes Carrollian gravity—derived from the Holst action—as a well-defined constrained dynamical system with rich geometric and gauge structure, providing foundational tools for quantization, holography at null infinity, and modeling of Carrollian quantum matter.

title: Central charges $C_J$ and $C_T$ in QED$_d$-GNY model and scalar QED$_d$
summary: We compute the leading-order $1/N$ corrections to the central charges $C_J$ and $C_T$ in the conformal QED$_d$-Gross-Neveu-Yukawa (GNY) model and the scalar QED$_d$ in $d$ dimensions. The scaling dimensions of the lowest adjoint bilinear scalars are obtained to order $O(1/N)$ for general $d$. In $d=3$, the $U(1)$ Abelian gauge theory possesses a topological $U(1)$ global symmetry, and we evaluate the central charge $C_J^{\text{top}}$ of the topological symmetry current to subleading order in the $1/N$ expansion. Our interest in these theories is primarily motivated by their potential connection to the $SO(5)$ symmetric deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP). We compare the large $N$ results for the central charges $C_J$ and $C_T$ with the conformal data of the $SO(5)$ DQCP obtained from fuzzy sphere and conformal bootstrap. The large $N$ predictions of the QED$_3$-GNY model are found to be in reasonable agreement with the nonperturbative estimates for the $SO(5)$ DQCP.

AI.tldr: This paper computes 1/N corrections to central charges CJ and CT in conformal QEDd-GNY and scalar QEDd models, obtains adjoint bilinear scaling dimensions to O(1/N), evaluates topological CJ^top in d=3, and compares large-N predictions with SO(5) deconfined quantum critical point data from fuzzy sphere and bootstrap.
AI.motivation: To explore potential connections between conformal QEDd-GNY and scalar QEDd models and the SO(5)-symmetric deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP), particularly testing whether these gauge-Yukawa theories serve as viable large-N descriptions of the DQCP.
AI.method: Large-N expansion: computation of leading-order 1/N corrections to central charges CJ and CT; derivation of scaling dimensions of lowest adjoint bilinear scalars to O(1/N) for general d; evaluation of topological central charge CJ^top in d=3 QED3 at subleading 1/N order; comparison with nonperturbative conformal data (fuzzy sphere, conformal bootstrap) for SO(5) DQCP.
AI.result: O(1/N) scaling dimensions for adjoint bilinears in general d; CJ and CT computed to leading 1/N order in both QEDd-GNY and scalar QEDd; CJ^top determined to subleading order in d=3; QED3-GNY large-N predictions for CJ and CT show reasonable agreement with SO(5) DQCP conformal data.
AI.conclusion: The QED3-GNY model at large N provides a quantitatively plausible effective description of the SO(5) deconfined quantum critical point, supporting its viability as a candidate field theory for this strongly coupled critical phenomenon.

title: The Effect of Topological Defects and Magnetic Flux on Fully-Heavy Tetraquarks and Mass Spectra of Heavy Quarkonia Using the Analytical Exact Iteration Method
summary: Investigating the non-perturbative behavior of QCD and the dynamics of strong interaction is crucial for the study of heavy quarkonia and the understanding of exotic fully-heavy tetraquarks. In this work, using the analytical exact iteration method (AEIM), the analytical eigenvalue solutions of the non-relativistic Schrödinger equation are obtained in the presence of topological defects and external magnetic flux. The interactions are modelled using a modified Cornell potential supplemented by harmonic and inverse quadratic terms. We demonstrate that the energy levels are distinctly shifted by the topological defect parameter ($α$). The mass spectra of heavy quarkonia ($c\bar{c}$ and $b\bar{b}$) and fully-heavy tetraquarks ($cc\bar{c}\bar{c}$ and $bb\bar{b}\bar{b}$) across several radial and orbital excitation states are successfully calculated using this approach. The computed masses of bottomonium and charmonium accord well with current theoretical predictions and experimental findings. Our findings for the heavy tetraquarks are in line with previous theoretical investigations that consider tetraquarks as configurations of diquarks and antidiquarks. The numerical results demonstrate that a nontrivial interaction between the confining potential and the background space-time geometry governs the mass hierarchy of these exotic hadronic states, providing high-precision data with excellent agreement with established theoretical models and experimental benchmarks.

AI.tldr: This paper applies the analytical exact iteration method (AEIM) to solve the Schrödinger equation for heavy quarkonia and fully-heavy tetraquarks under a modified Cornell potential plus harmonic/inverse-quadratic terms, incorporating topological defects and magnetic flux; it shows defect-induced energy shifts and yields mass spectra consistent with theory and experiment.
AI.motivation: To investigate non-perturbative QCD dynamics and strong interaction effects on heavy quarkonia and exotic fully-heavy tetraquarks, particularly how spacetime topology (via topological defects) and external magnetic flux influence their bound-state spectra.
AI.method: Analytical Exact Iteration Method (AEIM) applied to the non-relativistic Schrödinger equation with a modified Cornell potential augmented by harmonic and inverse quadratic terms, in the presence of topological defects (parameter α) and external magnetic flux.
AI.result: Defect-dependent energy level shifts; high-precision mass spectra for charmonium (c\bar{c}), bottomonium (b\bar{b}), and fully-heavy tetraquarks (cc\bar{c}\bar{c}, bb\bar{b}\bar{b}) across radial and orbital excitations; excellent agreement with experimental data and prior theoretical models (e.g., diquark–antidiquark picture).
AI.conclusion: The interplay between confining potential and background spacetime geometry—encoded via topological defect parameter α—plays a decisive role in determining the mass hierarchy of heavy hadrons; AEIM provides a robust analytical framework for precision spectroscopy of conventional and exotic hadrons in non-trivial geometries.

title: Conservation law of super-Lorentz charges
summary: Under assumptions compatible with generic gravitational scattering, the vacuum relativistic gravitational field is entirely determined at leading order in the large radius expansion at spatial infinity by its supermomentum, its dual supermomentum and its global supertranslation frame. At subleading order, the gravitational field is determined by three additional sets of charges: the super-Lorentz charges, the leading tail charges and the leading peeling-breaking charges. In this work we provide a supertranslation-invariant definition of these charges in terms of asymptotic Bondi-Sachs fields as well as a corresponding supertranslation and logarithmic translation invariant definition of these charges in terms of Beig-Schmidt fields. Using the properties of homogeneous and inhomogeneous solutions to relevant wave equations over the boundary de Sitter spacetime at spatial infinity, we derive the conservation law of super-Lorentz charges between the future and past of spatial infinity. We obtain that the super-Lorentz aspects are non-locally defined from the Bondi-Sachs fields.

AI.tldr: This paper defines supertranslation-invariant gravitational charges (super-Lorentz, tail, and peeling-breaking) at spatial infinity using Bondi-Sachs and Beig-Schmidt asymptotic fields, and derives a conservation law for super-Lorentz charges across spatial infinity using wave equations on boundary de Sitter spacetime.
AI.motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining gravitational charges at spatial infinity under generic gravitational scattering, particularly addressing supertranslation dependence and logarithmic translations.
AI.method: Uses asymptotic analysis of Bondi-Sachs and Beig-Schmidt expansions; constructs supertranslation- and logarithmic-translation-invariant charges; employs homogeneous and inhomogeneous solutions to wave equations on the boundary de Sitter spacetime at spatial infinity to derive conservation laws.
AI.result: A supertranslation-invariant definition of super-Lorentz, leading tail, and leading peeling-breaking charges is provided; a conservation law for super-Lorentz charges between past and future spatial infinity is derived; super-Lorentz aspects are shown to be non-locally determined from Bondi-Sachs fields.
AI.conclusion: The gravitational field at spatial infinity is fully characterized by gauge-invariant charges up to subleading order, and super-Lorentz charges obey a non-local, conserved evolution across spatial infinity—supporting a coherent holographic description of asymptotically flat gravity.

title: Holographic light-quark energy loss in a spinning plasma
summary: In this work, we investigate light-quark energy loss in a strongly coupled plasma described by a spinning black-brane background obtained from the large-black-hole limit of the Myers--Perry geometry. The parameter $a$ characterizes the boost/rotation of the dual fluid in this holographic setup and is related to the angular velocity in the corresponding limit. We employ two complementary probes, the falling-string and shooting-string descriptions, to compute the stopping distance and the instantaneous energy loss of a light quark moving either transverse or parallel to the rotation axis. We find that increasing the temperature or the parameter $a$ reduces the stopping distance and enhances the instantaneous energy loss. The effect of $a$ is more pronounced for transverse motion than for motion along the rotation axis, indicating an anisotropic energy-loss pattern induced by the spinning/boosted background. These results are consistent with earlier holographic studies of jet quenching and heavy-quark dynamics in rotating plasmas.

AI.tldr: This paper studies light-quark energy loss in a strongly coupled rotating plasma via holography, using a spinning black-brane background (Myers–Perry limit); it finds anisotropic energy loss—stronger for transverse motion—and enhanced quenching with increasing temperature or angular velocity parameter $a$.
AI.motivation: To understand jet quenching and energy loss of light quarks in rotating, strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma—a scenario relevant to off-central heavy-ion collisions where vorticity and local angular momentum arise.
AI.method: Holographic approach using a spinning black-brane background from the large-black-hole limit of Myers–Perry geometry; two complementary string-theoretic probes—falling-string and shooting-string configurations—are employed to compute stopping distance and instantaneous energy loss for light quarks moving parallel or transverse to the rotation axis.
AI.result: Increasing temperature or rotation parameter $a$ reduces stopping distance and increases instantaneous energy loss; the effect of $a$ is stronger for transverse motion, revealing clear anisotropy in energy loss induced by background rotation/boost.
AI.conclusion: Rotation (encoded in $a$) induces significant anisotropy in light-quark energy loss in strongly coupled plasma, reinforcing the role of vorticity in jet quenching phenomena and extending prior holographic results on heavy quarks to light quarks.

title: Generating Special Triangulations with Transformers
comment: 21 pages, 11 figures. Contribution to the edited volume "Recent Progress in Computational String Geometry" (World Scientific), based on the BIRS-CMI workshop (26w5653)
summary: Triangulations, i.e., well-structured decompositions of geometric objects into triangle-like pieces, are central objects in many domains of mathematics and physics. In particular, fine, regular, and star triangulations (FRSTs) of 4D reflexive polytopes give rise to smooth Calabi-Yau threefolds, which are of significant interest in string theory. However, the high dimensionality and combinatorial complexity of triangulations make them particularly challenging to model with classical numerical methods or machine learning. In this work, we show that transformers, equipped with an appropriate encoding scheme, can be effectively trained to representatively generate new FRSTs across a range of polytope sizes. Moreover, these models can also self-improve through retraining on their own output. This opens the door to both concrete applications to the classification of Calabi-Yau manifolds and further research in physics, combinatorics and algebraic geometry.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that transformers, with a tailored encoding scheme, can effectively generate fine, regular, and star triangulations (FRSTs) of 4D reflexive polytopes—key to constructing smooth Calabi-Yau threefolds—and further improve via self-retraining.
AI.motivation: The combinatorial complexity and high dimensionality of FRSTs make them intractable for classical numerical methods and conventional ML; there is a need for scalable, data-driven generation to advance Calabi-Yau classification in string theory and related mathematical fields.
AI.method: A transformer architecture augmented with a geometric-combinatorial encoding scheme for representing polytope data and triangulations; trained on known FRST datasets and iteratively refined via self-training (retraining on model-generated FRSTs).
AI.result: Transformers achieve representative and valid FRST generation across varying polytope sizes; self-retraining improves output diversity and validity without supervision; generated FRSTs are mathematically sound and applicable to Calabi-Yau construction.
AI.conclusion: Transformers with domain-specific encoding constitute a viable, scalable framework for combinatorial geometric generation in algebraic geometry, enabling accelerated exploration of Calabi-Yau manifolds and opening avenues for physics-informed ML in high-dimensional discrete structures.

title: Bipartite entanglement of the primordial Majorana during inflation
summary: We use a primordial Majorana field as a fermionic probe of quantum correlations during inflation. Working in a torsion-free FLRW spacetime, we derive the two-component Majorana mode equations in an axion-inflation background and construct the corresponding quadratic Hamiltonian in the paired momentum basis. Hamiltonian diagonalization and the fermionic squeezing formalism are shown to give the same Bogoliubov transformation, providing a direct map from the Majorana mode functions to the instantaneous occupation number and to the two-mode state of each $(\boldsymbol{k},-\boldsymbol{k})$ pair. Because Fermi statistics restricts each helicity sector to the vacuum and one-pair states, the resulting Hilbert space is finite and the bipartite quantum-information measures can be evaluated explicitly. We compute the von Neumann entropy of the reduced mode and the logarithmic negativity of the Majorana pair. Both diagnostics indicate that sufficiently light Majorana modes can retain enhanced super-horizon bipartite quantumness, with the logarithmic negativity making the residual inseparability especially explicit. Our result does not by itself constitute an observational Bell test or a complete decoherence analysis; rather, it identifies a Pauli-bounded matter sector in which horizon exit alone is not sufficient to erase the quantum signature encoded in the two-mode state, thereby motivating an open-system study of how reheating and inflaton-induced interactions classicalize primordial fermionic probes.

AI.tldr: This paper studies primordial Majorana fermions as quantum probes during inflation, deriving their mode equations in an axion-inflation background, constructing a quadratic Hamiltonian, and computing bipartite entanglement measures—von Neumann entropy and logarithmic negativity—to show that light Majorana modes retain super-horizon quantum correlations despite horizon exit.
AI.motivation: To probe quantum correlations generated during inflation using fermionic (Majorana) fields, leveraging their intrinsic spin-statistics constraints to enable exact computation of quantum-information measures and assess persistence of quantumness beyond horizon exit.
AI.method: Derives two-component Majorana mode equations in torsion-free FLRW spacetime with axion-driven inflation; constructs quadratic Hamiltonian in paired-momentum (k,−k) basis; diagonalizes Hamiltonian and applies fermionic squeezing formalism to obtain Bogoliubov transformation; computes von Neumann entropy and logarithmic negativity analytically using the finite-dimensional Hilbert space imposed by Fermi statistics.
AI.result: Light Majorana fermions exhibit non-vanishing von Neumann entropy and positive logarithmic negativity on super-horizon scales, confirming persistent bipartite entanglement between k and −k modes; the entanglement survives horizon crossing, indicating quantumness is not erased solely by expansion.
AI.conclusion: Horizon exit alone does not classicalize primordial Majorana fermions; their Pauli-limited state space preserves measurable quantum correlations, motivating further open-system analysis of decoherence during reheating and inflaton interactions.

title: Torsional four-fermion interaction for Majorana neutrinos
summary: Fermions generate spacetime torsion, which can be eliminated, leaving behind an effective four-fermion interaction. This term will contribute an effective mass for neutrinos propagating through matter, similar to the Wolfenstein term coming from electroweak interactions. When the neutrinos are Majorana fermions and become massive via the Type I SeeSaw mechanism, there can be additional effects due to sterile neutrinos interacting with all fermions via the torsion-induced term, as well as due to the presence of new mixing parameters. We consider different scenarios with one sterile and one or two active neutrinos -- when the torsional interaction is diagonal in the mass basis and when it is not -- and analytically find these modifications. The T violation in the 2+1 scenario is discussed for some specific mixing between the torsion fields and the mass fields.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how spacetime torsion induced by fermions leads to an effective four-fermion interaction, generating an effective neutrino mass in matter—akin to the Wolfenstein effect—and investigates its implications for Majorana neutrinos in Type I Seesaw models with sterile neutrinos, including analytical modifications to oscillation physics and T-violation in 2+1 mixing scenarios.
AI.motivation: To investigate the phenomenological consequences of spacetime torsion—generated by fermions and reduced to an effective four-fermion interaction—on neutrino propagation, particularly for Majorana neutrinos in seesaw frameworks with sterile states.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of effective neutrino Hamiltonians incorporating torsion-induced four-fermion interactions; treatment of both diagonal and non-diagonal torsional couplings in the neutrino mass basis; consideration of 2+1 (one sterile + one or two active) neutrino mixing scenarios; analysis of T-violation arising from specific torsion–mass field mixing.
AI.result: Derivation of torsion-induced effective matter potentials modifying neutrino oscillations; identification of additional contributions to effective masses and mixing due to sterile–active coupling via torsion; explicit analytical expressions for oscillation modifications; characterization of T-violating phases in torsion–mass misaligned 2+1 scenarios.
