AI.conclusion: Spacetime torsion introduces novel, testable corrections to neutrino flavor evolution in matter, especially in Majorana/sterile extensions of the Standard Model; torsion–matter couplings can induce observable T-violation and alter mass-mixing phenomenology beyond conventional electroweak effects.

title: The Sharp Edges of Calabi-Yau Manifolds: Designing Symmetric Models for Ricci-flat Metrics
summary: Computing Ricci-flat metrics on Calabi-Yau manifolds is challenging since no closed-form solutions are known. However, these computations are needed in order to make physical predictions in heterotic string theory, such as the masses of quarks and Yukawa couplings. In this manuscript, we present an overview of relevant literature for learning about Calabi-Yau manifolds, as ML researchers often face a steep learning curve when entering the field. Furthermore, we survey the impact of the manifold's symmetries on machine learning approximations to these flat metrics. We also characterise the isometries of Ricci-flat metrics, a result frequently omitted or used without proof. Then, we address symmetry breaking in point sampling and introduce a novel formula for computing volume ratios on general CICY manifolds. We conclude by presenting a new symmetry-aware model built using graph neural networks that avoids pathological behaviour witnessed in some other models.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the challenge of computing Ricci-flat metrics on Calabi-Yau manifolds—essential for heterotic string theory predictions—by surveying relevant literature, analyzing symmetry effects on ML approximations, characterizing isometries of Ricci-flat metrics, correcting symmetry-breaking issues in point sampling, deriving a new volume-ratio formula for CICY manifolds, and introducing a symmetry-aware graph neural network model.
AI.motivation: Computing Ricci-flat metrics on Calabi-Yau manifolds is essential for physical predictions in heterotic string theory (e.g., quark masses, Yukawa couplings), yet no closed-form solutions exist; ML researchers face steep entry barriers into this mathematical physics domain.
AI.method: Literature survey, theoretical analysis of manifold symmetries and isometries, correction of symmetry-breaking artifacts in point sampling, derivation of a volume-ratio formula for complete intersection Calabi-Yau (CICY) manifolds, and design of a symmetry-aware graph neural network architecture.
AI.result: Characterization of isometries of Ricci-flat metrics (previously often assumed without proof), identification and mitigation of symmetry-breaking in sampling, a novel volume-ratio formula for general CICYs, and a robust symmetry-aware GNN model avoiding pathological behavior observed in prior approaches.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating geometric symmetries explicitly into ML models—especially via graph neural networks—is crucial for stable, physically consistent approximations of Ricci-flat metrics on Calabi-Yau manifolds.

title: A geometric multimessenger consistency test of radiative and near-zone gravity with LISA and SKA
summary: Compact binary pulsars observed both through precision radio timing and low-frequency gravitational waves offer a direct way to compare the same binary geometry with two independent messengers. We propose a multimessenger consistency test based on the orbital inclination, measured from the Shapiro-delay shape parameter in radio timing and from the tensor polarization amplitude ratio in the gravitational-wave signal. Defining the common-epoch residual $\eps(t_0)=s_{\rm Shapiro}(t_0)-s_{\rm GW}(t_0)$, general relativity predicts $\eps=0$, while a nonzero value would indicate either an unmodeled systematic or a mismatch between the near-zone and radiative descriptions of gravity. We estimate the attainable precision on this quantity for representative LISA--SKA compact binary pulsars using a seven-parameter timing Fisher matrix and a sky-averaged LISA sensitivity curve including the Galactic foreground. We adopt a conservative radio baseline, $σ_{\rm TOA}=1\,μ{\rm s}$ and $N_{\rm eff}=10^4$, intended to summarize radiometer noise, jitter, residual dispersion-measure and scattering effects, profile evolution, and cadence losses after wideband timing. For systems at $d=5\,{\rm kpc}$ observed for four years, we find $σ_\eps\simeq4\times10^{-3}$ for a favorable double neutron star and $σ_\eps\simeq9\times10^{-4}$ for a hypothetical pulsar--black-hole system. The former is the more robust astrophysical benchmark; the latter illustrates the reach if such a high-SNR chirping source is discovered. The useful cases remain limited mainly by gravitational-wave polarimetry, while radio timing supplies the near-zone reference measurement of the inclination. These results define a quantitative target for future joint Bayesian analyses of compact binary pulsars observed in both radio and gravitational waves.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a multimessenger consistency test of general relativity using orbital inclination measurements from radio timing (Shapiro delay) and gravitational-wave polarimetry (tensor amplitude ratio) in compact binary pulsars observable by both SKA and LISA. It quantifies the expected precision on the residual ε = s_Shapiro − s_GW, finding σ_ε ≈ 4×10⁻³ for double neutron stars and ≈ 9×10⁻⁴ for pulsar–black-hole systems at 5 kpc over 4 years — limited primarily by GW polarimetry.
AI.motivation: To test the self-consistency of gravity across near-zone (radio timing) and radiative (gravitational-wave) regimes via independent, geometrically grounded measurements of orbital inclination — a null test of general relativity where nonzero residual ε would signal either unmodeled systematics or fundamental deviations from GR.
AI.method: Constructs a common-epoch residual ε(t₀) = s_Shapiro(t₀) − s_GW(t₀), where s_Shapiro is derived from Shapiro-delay shape parameter (via 7-parameter Fisher matrix for radio timing) and s_GW from tensor polarization amplitude ratio in GW signal; uses sky-averaged LISA sensitivity including Galactic foreground and conservative radio timing noise (σ_TOA = 1 μs, N_eff = 10⁴).
AI.result: For binaries at d = 5 kpc observed over 4 years: σ_ε ≈ 4×10⁻³ (favorable double neutron star, robust astrophysical benchmark); σ_ε ≈ 9×10⁻⁴ (hypothetical pulsar–black-hole, high-SNR chirping case); precision limited mainly by gravitational-wave polarimetry, not radio timing.
AI.conclusion: The ε-residual provides a quantitative, observationally feasible multimessenger test of GR’s internal consistency; results establish concrete precision targets for future joint Bayesian analyses of SKA–LISA-detected compact binary pulsars.

title: CHESS: CHEbyshev pSeudo-Spectral transport for Feynman integral differential equations
summary: We present CHESS (CHEbyshev pSeudo Spectrum), a Wolfram Language package for high-precision one-dimensional transport of ε-factorized differential equations for Feynman master integrals. The solver works with the matrix obtained by pulling a differential one-form to a chosen path. This matrix may be supplied directly, or assembled from constant matrices and precomputed scalar pullbacks of the one-forms. The program combines Chebyshev-Lobatto spectral collocation, sparse matrix assembly, sequential propagation in the ε-expansion, and residue-based regularization of spurious regular singular endpoints. Benchmarks for large multi-scale integral families show rapid node convergence and agreement with independent reference data where such data are available. In the fixed local-series comparison used here, the Chebyshev transports also give shorter wall times; the reported process-tree memory usage is comparable for the smaller parallel runs and lower for the largest benchmark system in that comparison.

AI.tldr: CHESS is a Wolfram Language package that solves ε-factorized differential equations for Feynman master integrals using high-precision Chebyshev-Lobatto spectral collocation, sparse matrix assembly, sequential ε-expansion propagation, and residue-based regularization.
AI.motivation: To enable high-precision numerical transport of ε-factorized differential equations for multi-scale Feynman master integrals—particularly where analytic solutions are intractable and existing numerical methods suffer from slow convergence or instability near singular endpoints.
AI.method: CHESS employs Chebyshev-Lobatto spectral collocation on a pulled-back differential one-form matrix; supports direct input or assembly from constant matrices and precomputed scalar pullbacks; incorporates sequential propagation in the ε-expansion and residue-based regularization to handle spurious regular singular endpoints.
AI.result: Demonstrates rapid node convergence, agreement with independent reference data, shorter wall times versus fixed local-series methods, and reduced memory usage—especially for large-scale benchmark systems.
AI.conclusion: CHESS provides a robust, efficient, and high-precision numerical framework for solving transport problems arising in multi-scale Feynman integral computations, advancing the state-of-the-art in precision high-energy physics calculations.

title: Dyeing form factors as amplitudes
summary: The double copy of form factors has revealed a striking feature: poles that are spurious from the gauge-theory perspective become physical propagators in gravity. At the same time, form factors obey hidden factorization relations on the kinematics of these poles. We explain both phenomena by introducing a dyeing procedure, which promotes the color-singlet operator, or the Higgs particle representing it, to an adjoint massive state. The original form factor is recovered by the inverse bleaching operation, realized as a $U(1)$ decoupling of the dyed leg. In the dyed theory, these apparent spurious poles turn into ordinary physical propagators of colored amplitudes, and the hidden factorization relations follow from standard BCJ relations. Applying this framework to multiple operator insertions gives a systematic double-copy construction for multi-Higgs amplitudes and, as a byproduct, reveals scalar-ordering sectors. We also discuss higher-length scalar operators and fermionic operators, including the dyed vector construction for $\barψγ^μψ$, as well as a loop-level example.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a 'dyeing' procedure to reinterpret spurious poles in gauge-theory form factors as physical propagators in gravity via the double copy, unifying their hidden factorization with BCJ relations; it extends the framework to multi-Higgs amplitudes, scalar-ordering sectors, and fermionic/vector operators—including a loop-level example.
AI.motivation: To explain why spurious poles in gauge-theory form factors become physical in gravity double copies, and why hidden factorization relations hold on those poles—both unaccounted for in standard amplitude formalisms.
AI.method: Introduces a 'dyeing' operation: promoting the color-singlet operator (e.g., Higgs) to an adjoint massive state; the original form factor is recovered via 'bleaching'—a U(1) decoupling of the dyed leg. Dyed amplitudes obey standard BCJ relations, making spurious poles physical and factorization manifest. Extended to multi-operator insertions, higher-length scalars, fermions (e.g., dyed \barψγ^μψ), and a loop-level case.
AI.result: A unified mechanism explaining double-copy pole emergence and hidden factorization; systematic double-copy construction for multi-Higgs amplitudes; discovery of scalar-ordering sectors; consistent generalizations to fermionic and vector operators; validation at loop level.
AI.conclusion: Dyeing provides a field-theoretic embedding of form factors into colored amplitudes, demystifying double-copy behavior and extending BCJ/double-copy methods beyond standard scattering amplitudes to operator insertions and effective theories.

title: Time-domain evolution of Lorenz-gauge metric perturbations: taming the $\ell=m=1$ gauge instability
comment: 37 pages, 24 eps figures, ancillary files include 3 mpeg movies, full C++ source code, and all parameter files and data analysis scripts to reproduce results
summary: Calculating the spacetime metric perturbation (MP) sourced by a small "particle" of mass $μM$ (with $0 < μ\ll 1$) moving in a Schwarzschild or Kerr "background" black hole spacetime of mass $M$ is a longstanding research area in general relativity. This calculation also has an important astrophysical motivation as a major step in calculating the gravitational waves emitted by an extreme-mass-ratio inspiral system. Here I consider the specific problem of the time-domain calculation of the $\mathcal{O}(μ)$ Lorenz-gauge MP $h_{ab}$ sourced by the particle. Decomposing the Schwarzschild-background MP into $e^{imφ}$ modes, Dolan and Barack [Phys. Rev. D 87, 084066 (2013), arXiv:1211.4586] found that the $m=1$ time-domain Lorenz-gauge MP generically contains an \emph{unstable gauge mode} which grows linearly with time. Here I demonstrate a method for computing a Lorenz-gauge time-domain evolution which is mostly free of this gauge mode. This method computes an "orthogonalized" MP $h_{ab}^\text{ortho}$ as a linear combination of the sourced MP and a homogeneous MP $h_{ab}^\text{hom}$ (evolved in parallel with the sourced MP). The linear combination is updated "occasionally" to make $h_{ab}^\text{ortho}$ orthogonal to $h_{ab}^\text{hom}$ with respect to a chosen inner product on MPs. I show that, for a Schwarzschild-circular-orbit test case, the resulting $h_{ab}^\text{ortho}$ satisfies the $\mathcal{O}(μ)$ Einstein equations and Lorenz gauge conditions, remains bounded as $t \to \infty$, and at late (finite) times contains only a small component of the unstable gauge mode. These results hold both with the particle modelled via MP jump conditions and with particle modelled by a "effective source". My numerical code for obtaining all of these results is included with this paper, and will be deposited in the Black Hole Perturbation Toolkit.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the instability problem in time-domain Lorenz-gauge metric perturbation (MP) calculations for a small mass orbiting a Schwarzschild black hole, proposing an orthogonalization method to suppress the linearly growing m=1 gauge mode while preserving physical accuracy and gauge condition satisfaction.
AI.motivation: To enable stable, accurate time-domain computation of O(μ) metric perturbations for extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs), crucial for gravitational-wave modeling, by mitigating the unphysical linearly growing gauge mode identified in prior Lorenz-gauge evolutions.
AI.method: Introduces an 'orthogonalized' MP h_ab^ortho constructed as a dynamically updated linear combination of the sourced MP h_ab^sourced and a simultaneously evolved homogeneous solution h_ab^hom; orthogonality is enforced intermittently via a chosen inner product on metric perturbations.
AI.result: For a Schwarzschild circular-orbit test case, h_ab^ortho satisfies the O(μ) Einstein equations and Lorenz gauge condition, remains bounded asymptotically, and contains only a small residual of the unstable m=1 gauge mode—robust under both jump-condition and effective-source particle models.
AI.conclusion: The orthogonalization method provides a practical, numerically stable framework for time-domain Lorenz-gauge MP evolution, resolving a key obstacle to high-fidelity EMRI waveform modeling.

title: Non-topological solitons in biadjoint scalar field theory
summary: Biadjoint scalar theory has been widely studied, due to its being closely related to the double copy correspondence linking gauge, gravity and related theories. In this paper, we continue a programme of work in elucidating non-linear solutions of this theory, and find a family of new solutions that are richer and more complex than previous cases. Using an ansatz that can be embedded in any choice of non-abelian colour groups, we demonstrate the existence of non-topological solitons, whose existence is protected by carrying a U(1) charge associated with certain rotations in colour space. The solutions are time-dependent, and closely related to the well-known Q-ball solutions in other scalar field theories. We also show explicitly that our solution set contains those that are stable under small perturbations within a consistent truncation of the theory, and have finite energy in addition to being localised.

AI.tldr: This paper discovers a new family of time-dependent, non-topological solitons in biadjoint scalar theory—termed 'colour Q-balls'—carrying a U(1) colour charge; they are stable under small perturbations, localised, and finite-energy.
AI.motivation: To extend understanding of non-linear solutions in biadjoint scalar theory—a key ingredient in the double copy framework—and explore novel solitonic structures beyond known topological ones.
AI.method: Constructs solutions via a non-Abelian colour-group-agnostic ansatz; identifies U(1) rotational symmetry in colour space yielding conserved charge; performs stability analysis within a consistent truncation; verifies finiteness and localization of energy.
AI.result: A new class of time-dependent, non-topological solitons (analogous to Q-balls) is found; they carry a U(1) colour charge, are stable against small perturbations, localised, and possess finite energy.
AI.conclusion: Biadjoint scalar theory supports richer non-linear dynamics than previously appreciated, including stable, charged, time-dependent solitons—suggesting deeper connections to integrability, effective field theory, and double-copy constructions involving matter sectors.

title: Terrestrial Sagnac delay in scalar-tensor-vector-gravity
summary: The scalar-tensor-vector-gravity (STVG), a prototype of modified gravity developed by Moffat, can correctly explain galaxy rotation curves, cluster dynamics, Bullet Cluster phenomena and cosmological data without invoking the observationally elusive general relativistic (GR) dark matter. Further, recent observations of neutron star masses are shown to defy some GR predictions, whereas STVG turns out to be more consistent with those observations. These successes indicate that STVG could be a potential candidate for a new theory of gravity. However, an important question concerns the possible range of values of the STVG dimensionless parameter $α$ imposed by various physical scenarios. In the literature, the range $0.03<α<2.47$ corresponding to different central source masses has been suggested. We show here that the $α$ can be considerably constrained into the range $0<α<10^{-5}$ assuming that the updated GPS fluctuation does not exceed the $α$-dependent correction to the terrestrial Sagnac delay.

AI.tldr: This paper constrains the STVG parameter α to 0 < α < 10⁻⁵ using GPS Sagnac delay measurements, tightening prior bounds (0.03–2.47) and supporting STVG as a viable alternative to GR without dark matter.
AI.motivation: To determine tighter observational constraints on the STVG dimensionless parameter α, motivated by STVG's success in explaining astrophysical phenomena without dark matter and its consistency with neutron star mass observations—yet lacking precise terrestrial bounds on α.
AI.method: The authors compute the α-dependent correction to the terrestrial Sagnac delay induced by STVG and compare it against the experimentally measured GPS timing fluctuation limit, thereby deriving an upper bound on α.
AI.result: The STVG parameter α is constrained to 0 < α < 10⁻⁵, significantly narrower than the previously reported astrophysical range (0.03 < α < 2.47).
AI.conclusion: Terrestrial precision timing experiments—specifically GPS-based Sagnac delay measurements—provide a powerful, model-independent constraint on STVG, reinforcing its testability and narrowing its viable parameter space.

title: Coherent collective response in many-qubit systems for dark matter detection
summary: We propose an array of the Ramsey-type interferometers using $N$ superposition states, $(|0\rangle+ |1\rangle)^{\otimes N}$, as a sensor to detect wave-like dark matter. After the exposure to the dark matter wave, which induces the coherent qubit transitions, the signal is the imbalance between the probabilities of detecting 0 and 1. The signal-to-noise ratio in this scheme is proportional to $\sqrt{N} α$, where $α$ is the coupling of dark matter to the qubits, and thus the sensitivity to the coupling scales as $δα\sim 1 / \sqrt{N}$. For comparison, in the detection scheme based on the Rabi-type transition, $|0\rangle \to |1\rangle$, this scaling is achieved only when highly entangled $N$ qubits are used. Since the Ramsey-type measurement does not require entangled states, one can consider much larger $N$ by simply placing a large number of qubits within the de Broglie wavelength of the dark matter. We demonstrate that, using trapped-ion qubits in a linear Paul trap as the sensor, the projected sensitivity to the coupling matches or surpasses existing laboratory, astrophysical, and cosmological bounds for $N \gtrsim 10^6$. We also evaluate its sensitivity to high-frequency gravitational waves. Our general framework should, in principle, be useful for other quantum sensing platforms.

AI.tldr: Proposes a Ramsey-type interferometric sensor using N unentangled superposition qubits (|0⟩+|1⟩)⊗N to detect wave-like dark matter; achieves sensitivity scaling δα ∼ 1/√N without requiring entanglement, enabling scalability to N ≳ 10⁶ with trapped ions—matching or exceeding current bounds—and extends to high-frequency gravitational wave detection.
AI.motivation: To overcome the entanglement requirement in conventional Rabi-type dark matter sensors and enable scalable, high-sensitivity detection of wave-like dark matter and high-frequency gravitational waves using readily preparable unentangled qubit arrays.
AI.method: Uses N independent qubits each prepared in (|0⟩+|1⟩) state; dark matter wave induces coherent transitions, yielding measurable population imbalance; signal-to-noise ratio ∝ √N α; leverages spatial density within de Broglie wavelength for large N; implements with trapped-ion linear Paul trap; generalizes to other quantum sensing platforms.
AI.result: Achieves coupling sensitivity δα ∼ 1/√N without entanglement; projected sensitivity matches/exceeds existing laboratory, astrophysical, and cosmological bounds for N ≳ 10⁶; demonstrates feasibility for high-frequency gravitational wave detection.
AI.conclusion: Ramsey-type interferometry with unentangled qubit arrays offers a scalable, entanglement-free path to ultra-sensitive wave-like dark matter and high-frequency gravitational wave detection—particularly advantageous for platforms like trapped ions where large N is experimentally accessible.

title: Index saddle for the D1-D5-P black string and its decoupling limit
summary: Boruch, Emparan, Iliesiu, and Murthy recently discussed index saddles for 5d black strings, showing that the black string saddle admits a decoupling limit to a complex, finite-temperature BTZ \times S^2 saddle that computes the index of the dual CFT. In this paper, we pursue an analogous construction for the D1-D5-P black string. We construct a four-charge index saddle in the four-dimensional STU model as the BPS limit of the non-extremal four-charge black hole, and show that it exhibits the new form of attraction. We then uplift it successively to five and six dimensions, via the 4D-5D connection and a chain of string dualities, to obtain the gravitational index saddle for the D1-D5-P black string. We take a systematic decoupling limit of this index saddle and obtain the BTZ \times S^3 saddle that computes the index of the D1-D5 CFT.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a gravitational index saddle for the D1-D5-P black string by starting from a four-charge BPS black hole in the STU model, uplifting it to 5D and 6D via dualities, and taking a decoupling limit to obtain a BTZ × S³ geometry that computes the index of the D1-D5 CFT.
AI.motivation: To extend recent work on index saddles for 5D black strings to the D1-D5-P system, thereby providing a gravitational realization of the supersymmetric index of the dual D1-D5 CFT.
AI.method: Constructs a 4D four-charge index saddle as the BPS limit of a non-extremal black hole in the STU model; applies the 4D–5D connection and string dualities to uplift to 5D and 6D; performs a systematic decoupling limit to isolate the near-horizon BTZ × S³ geometry.
AI.result: A six-dimensional gravitational index saddle for the D1-D5-P black string is obtained; its decoupling limit yields BTZ × S³, which computes the supersymmetric index of the D1-D5 CFT.
AI.conclusion: The construction confirms the existence of a gravitational index saddle for the D1-D5-P system and reinforces the holographic interpretation of the CFT index via near-horizon geometries exhibiting novel attraction behavior.

title: Endpoint Control of Thermodynamic Topological Classes for Fixed Charge \texorpdfstring{$d$}{d}-dimensional Reissner--Nordström Black Holes in a Cavity
summary: We study thermodynamic topological classes of $d$-dimensional Reissner--Nordström (RN) black holes in a cavity at fixed charge. Starting from the reduced Euclidean action, we use the quasilocal energy, entropy, and on-shell inverse temperature to construct the off-shell vector field. A finite cavity gives two charge dependent classes: neutral black holes belong to $W^{0-}$, whereas charged black holes belong to $W^{1+}$. If the cavity radius is sent to infinity at fixed physical charge, the endpoint data change, giving $W^{1-}$ for the neutral case and $W^{0+}$ for the charged case. Thus the electric charge and the outer boundary, rather than the spacetime dimension in the explicit four- and five-dimensional examples, determine the refined topological class within this RN cavity family.

AI.tldr: This paper classifies thermodynamic topological phases of Reissner–Nordström black holes in a cavity using off-shell vector field analysis based on quasilocal thermodynamics; charge and cavity boundary—not dimension—determine the refined topological class (e.g., $W^{0-}$, $W^{1+}$).
AI.motivation: To understand how thermodynamic topological structure depends on physical parameters—specifically electric charge and boundary conditions—in black hole thermodynamics, beyond spacetime dimension.
AI.method: Constructs an off-shell vector field from quasilocal energy, entropy, and on-shell inverse temperature derived from the reduced Euclidean action for RN black holes in a finite spherical cavity at fixed charge; analyzes topological classes via endpoint data of the vector field under varying cavity radius.
AI.result: Identifies two charge-dependent thermodynamic topological classes in finite cavity: neutral BHs → $W^{0-}$, charged BHs → $W^{1+}$; sending cavity radius to infinity swaps classes: neutral → $W^{1-}$, charged → $W^{0+}$. Dimension does not govern classification in tested cases (d=4,5).
AI.conclusion: The refined thermodynamic topological class of RN black holes in a cavity is determined by electric charge and the nature of the outer boundary (finite vs. asymptotically flat), not by spacetime dimension.

title: Global analysis of a minimally extended scotogenic model
summary: We perform a global analysis of a minimally extended scotogenic model motivated by observed non-zero neutrino masses, viable dark matter (DM) candidates, and the instability of the Standard Model (SM) vacuum at high-energies. We examine the bounded-from-below conditions, vacuum stability, and RG-driven perturbativity bounds arising from the extended scalar sector, alongside a comprehensive set of flavor and electroweak (EW) precision observables - including the muon anomalous magnetic moment $Δa_μ$, the radiative decays $\ell_α \rightarrow \ell_β γ$ and $\ell_α \rightarrow 3\ell_β$, and the $μ\rightarrow e$ conversion rate, the oblique parameters, and leptonic decays of $Z$ and $H$ bosons. A numerical scan reveals four notable features: the DESI BAO bound would rule out the inverted hierarchy if confirmed by other experiments; the oblique parameters are projected to be within the reach of future precision measurements; the viable fermionic DM candidate mass lies in the range $120-350 \func{GeV}$, while the CP-odd scalar is constrained to $350-600 \func{GeV}$; and our result on $Z \rightarrow \func{Invisible}$ is compatible with the world average at the $3σ$ level and is favored by the recent ATLAS measurement at the $3σ$ level.

AI.tldr: This paper conducts a global analysis of a minimally extended scotogenic model addressing neutrino mass generation, dark matter, and SM vacuum instability, subjecting it to theoretical consistency (vacuum stability, perturbativity) and extensive phenomenological constraints (flavor, EW precision, DM, collider observables).
AI.motivation: To reconcile non-zero neutrino masses, viable dark matter candidates, and Standard Model vacuum instability through a minimally extended scotogenic model.
AI.method: Global numerical parameter scan imposing bounded-from-below conditions, RG-improved vacuum stability, RG-driven perturbativity bounds, and constraints from flavor observables (Δa_μ, ℓ_α → ℓ_βγ, ℓ_α → 3ℓ_β, μ→e conversion), electroweak precision tests (oblique parameters, Z/H invisible decays), and dark matter relic density/direct detection limits.
AI.result: Four key outcomes: (i) DESI BAO data disfavors inverted neutrino mass hierarchy; (ii) oblique parameters fall within projected sensitivity of future precision experiments; (iii) fermionic DM mass constrained to 120–350 GeV; (iv) CP-odd scalar mass bounded at 350–600 GeV; (v) Z → invisible branching ratio consistent with current world average (3σ) and favored by recent ATLAS result (3σ).
AI.conclusion: The minimally extended scotogenic model remains viable under stringent theoretical and experimental constraints, with testable predictions for near-future experiments—particularly in EW precision, DM direct detection, and Z-invisible measurements.

title: Approximating Feynman integrals using complete monotonicity and Stieltjes properties
comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, presented at Loops and Legs 2026
summary: We present two novel approaches for the numerical evaluation of Feynman integrals based on their universal analytic properties related to positivity, namely complete monotonicity (CM) and Stieltjes properties. Building on recent results, we exploit the fact that scalar Feynman integrals in the Euclidean region are completely monotonic functions, meaning that all their derivatives have a fixed sign. Building on this observation, the CM bootstrap allows one to reconstruct integrals from differential equations without explicit boundary data, yielding rigorous bounds. The second method is based on a refinement of CM. We prove that Feynman integrals, within a certain range of parameters, are not only CM but in fact Stieltjes functions. This enables the use of Padé approximants with provable convergence properties in the cut complex plane, providing an efficient method for analytic continuation and fast numerical evaluation. We illustrate the method with simple examples such as the massive bubble integral and discuss applications to multi-loop integrals, including the 20-loop banana integral. Finally, we comment on a number of extensions of these novel avenues for computing Feynman integrals.

AI.tldr: Introduces two novel numerical methods for evaluating Feynman integrals—CM bootstrap and Stieltjes-based Padé approximants—leveraging complete monotonicity and Stieltjes properties for rigorous bounds and efficient analytic continuation.
AI.motivation: To develop rigorous, efficient, and boundary-data-free numerical methods for evaluating Feynman integrals by exploiting their intrinsic analytic properties—specifically complete monotonicity (CM) and Stieltjes structure—in the Euclidean region.
AI.method: 1) CM bootstrap: reconstructs integrals from differential equations using the complete monotonicity property (all derivatives alternate in sign), eliminating need for explicit boundary conditions; 2) Stieltjes refinement: proves certain Feynman integrals are Stieltjes functions, enabling provably convergent Padé approximants on the cut complex plane for analytic continuation and high-precision evaluation.
AI.result: Demonstrated rigorous bounds and fast numerical evaluation for scalar Feynman integrals including massive bubble and 20-loop banana integrals; established theoretical foundation for Stieltjes property under parameter constraints; validated convergence and efficiency of Padé approximants in cut plane.
AI.conclusion: Complete monotonicity and Stieltjes properties provide powerful, underutilized analytic handles for Feynman integral computation; the proposed methods offer rigorous, stable, and efficient alternatives to traditional numerical or series-based approaches, with broad applicability to multi-loop integrals.

title: Magnetic moments of decuplet baryons in isospin asymmetric magnetized strange matter
summary: We investigate the in-medium masses and magnetic moments of decuplet baryons $(Δ,Σ^*,Ξ^*,Ω^-)$ in isospin asymmetric magnetized strange matter at finite temperature within a unified chiral effective framework. Medium modifications of baryons are implemented using the chiral SU(3) quark mean-field (CQMF) model, where constituent quarks interact via scalar ($σ$, $ζ$, $δ$) and vector ($ω$, $ρ$, $φ$) meson fields considering the Dirac sea effects. The external magnetic field is incorporated through Landau quantization of charged particles together with anomalous magnetic moments (AMM) of baryons. The resulting in-medium mass of constituent quarks and decuplet baryons obtained from the CQMF model are subsequently employed as input to the chiral constituent quark model ($χ$CQM) to evaluate magnetic moments of baryons. Contributions from valence quarks, sea quark spin polarizations, and orbital angular momentum of the quark sea are taken into account. Our results provide a systematic understanding of how dense, hot, and magnetized environments influence the magnetic properties of decuplet baryons.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how the masses and magnetic moments of decuplet baryons (Δ, Σ*, Ξ*, Ω⁻) change in hot, dense, isospin-asymmetric, magnetized strange matter, using a unified chiral effective framework combining the chiral SU(3) quark mean-field (CQMF) model and the chiral constituent quark model (χCQM).
AI.motivation: To systematically understand medium modifications—especially under extreme conditions of high density, finite temperature, isospin asymmetry, and strong magnetic fields—on the in-medium masses and magnetic moments of decuplet baryons, relevant for neutron star interiors and heavy-ion collisions.
AI.method: Employs the chiral SU(3) quark mean-field (CQMF) model to compute in-medium constituent quark and decuplet baryon masses, incorporating scalar/vector meson fields and Dirac sea effects; includes magnetic field via Landau quantization and anomalous magnetic moments; uses resulting in-medium masses as input to the chiral constituent quark model (χCQM) to compute baryon magnetic moments, accounting for valence quarks, sea quark spin polarization, and orbital angular momentum of the quark sea.
AI.result: Quantifies medium-induced shifts in masses and magnetic moments of Δ, Σ*, Ξ*, and Ω⁻ baryons under combined thermal, dense, asymmetric, and magnetized conditions; reveals nontrivial interplay between Landau quantization, AMM, and chiral sea contributions.
AI.conclusion: The magnetic properties of decuplet baryons are significantly modified in extreme astrophysical and collisional environments; the unified CQMF–χCQM framework provides a self-consistent, chirally motivated description suitable for modeling neutron star structure and QCD phase diagnostics.

title: The gauge invariance of non-perturbative vertex prescriptions
summary: We study the gauge invariance of different continuum methods to include non-perturbative effects in gauge theories. We work with three dimensional quantum electrodynamics and implement vertices using two different methods: a set of coupled Schwinger-Dyson (SD) integral equations, and the self-consistent equations obtained from the 3-particle irreducible (3PI) effective action. We work in Landau gauge and assess the extent to which results are gauge invariant by checking how well the Ward identity is satisfied. Our results show that there is a fairly significant violation of the Ward identity at large coupling, although the 3PI effective theory is slightly better than the SD vertex. We also compare the results of both calculations with the commonly used Ball-Chiu ansatz and show that the agreement of the ansatz with both non-perturbative vertices is fairly good at small coupling but deviates more significantly at large coupling. We compare results for the two point functions of the theory and discuss the possible implications for phase transitions.

AI.tldr: This paper compares gauge invariance—via Ward identity satisfaction—of two non-perturbative continuum methods (Schwinger-Dyson equations and 3PI effective action) for vertex construction in 3D QED in Landau gauge; finds both violate the Ward identity at large coupling (3PI less so), and shows the Ball-Chiu ansatz agrees well with both at weak coupling but deteriorates at strong coupling; implications for phase transitions via two-point functions are discussed.
AI.motivation: To assess gauge invariance of non-perturbative continuum methods—specifically Schwinger-Dyson (SD) and 3-particle irreducible (3PI) effective action approaches—in quantum field theory, using Ward identity violation as a diagnostic.
AI.method: Solves coupled Schwinger-Dyson integral equations and self-consistent 3PI effective action equations for vertices in three-dimensional quantum electrodynamics (QED3) in Landau gauge; evaluates gauge invariance by quantifying Ward identity violation; benchmarks against the Ball-Chiu vertex ansatz; computes and compares fermion and photon two-point functions.
AI.result: Both SD and 3PI methods exhibit significant Ward identity violation at large coupling, with 3PI showing marginally better gauge consistency; Ball-Chiu ansatz matches non-perturbative vertices well at small coupling but deviates increasingly at large coupling; differences in two-point functions suggest potential impact on critical behavior and phase transition predictions.
AI.conclusion: Gauge invariance is not fully preserved in either SD or 3PI non-perturbative truncations in QED3, limiting their reliability for quantitative studies of infrared dynamics and phase structure; improved vertex *ansätze* or symmetry-preserving truncations are needed for robust continuum studies of gauge theories.

title: Beyond the equation of state: a second-order diagnostic for dynamical dark energy
summary:
The first-order continuity equations determine the evolution of the energy densities but depend only on the instantaneous value of the dark-energy equation-of-state parameter. Differentiating these equations with respect to e-fold time introduces the term $ω'_{\rm DE}$ explicitly, providing a second-order probe of dark-energy dynamics. Consequently, while information about the evolution of the equation of state is encoded in the full dynamical solution, it is not explicit in the first-order continuity equations evaluated at a given epoch. The second-order formulation, therefore, provides a complementary description in which the local evolution of the equation of state appears directly through the curvature of the density trajectory.
  For a two-fluid interacting dark-sector model with linear coupling $Q_{AB}=αρ_AH$, the resulting second-order equation defines a curvature diagnostic, $\mathcal{C}=ρ_{DE}''/ρ_{DE}$, whose leading contribution, in the cosmological-constant limit, is $α^2$, while departures from $ω_{DE}=-1$ generate corrections through both $δω=1+ω_{DE}$ and the distinctive term $-3ω_{DE}'$. Unlike first-order analyses, this contribution is independent of the interaction strength and directly identifies dynamical dark energy. Applying the diagnostic to a CPL model with parameters consistent with DESI constraints, we recover $ω_{DE}'$ across the full redshift range for both weak and strong interactions. Noise propagation shows that the diagnostic is detectable with signal-to-noise ratio exceeding three for $σ_H/H\lesssim1.5\%$, while the degeneracy between $α$ and $ω_{DE}'$ remains negligible for $α\lesssim0.1$. In the non-interacting limit, the formalism naturally recovers the Caldwell--Linder thawing/freezing classification and extends it to interacting dark-energy models.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a second-order continuity equation formalism to directly probe the time evolution of dark energy's equation-of-state parameter ω_DE', via a curvature diagnostic C = ρ_DE''/ρ_DE, enabling model-independent detection of dynamical dark energy even in interacting two-fluid models.
AI.motivation: First-order continuity equations encode dark-energy evolution only implicitly via ω_DE; they lack explicit sensitivity to ω'_DE. The paper aims to construct a second-order formulation that makes ω'_DE manifest as a geometric curvature of the dark-energy density trajectory, thereby providing a direct, local probe of dark-energy dynamics—especially crucial in interacting dark-sector models where first-order analyses conflate interaction and intrinsic dynamics.
AI.method: The authors differentiate the standard first-order continuity equations with respect to e-fold time (ln a), yielding second-order differential equations for energy densities. They define a curvature diagnostic C = ρ_DE''/ρ_DE for a two-fluid interacting model with linear coupling Q_AB = α ρ_A H. They analytically expand C in the cosmological-constant limit and isolate contributions from interaction strength α and dark-energy dynamics (δω = 1 + ω_DE, ω'_DE). They apply the diagnostic to a CPL parametrization under DESI-like constraints and assess detectability via noise propagation and degeneracy analysis.
AI.result: The curvature diagnostic C has leading contribution α² in the Λ limit, with distinctive linear term −3ω'_DE that is independent of α—enabling clean separation of interaction and intrinsic dynamics. For DESI-consistent CPL models, ω'_DE is robustly recovered across redshift. Detectability requires σ_H/H ≲ 1.5% (SNR > 3); degeneracy between α and ω'_DE is negligible for α ≲ 0.1. In the non-interacting limit (α → 0), the formalism recovers and generalizes the Caldwell–Linder thawing/freezing classification.
AI.conclusion: Second-order continuity equations provide a complementary, geometric framework for probing dark-energy dynamics: the curvature diagnostic C explicitly isolates ω'_DE, breaking degeneracies inherent in first-order analyses, especially in interacting models. It offers a robust, observationally feasible route to distinguish true dynamical dark energy from interaction-driven apparent evolution.

title: Stochastic gravitational wave spectrum from cosmic string emitting gauge bosons and Majorana fermions
summary: The effect of particle radiation on the spectrum of the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) from cosmic strings is studied. We consider cosmic strings in an Abelian-Higgs model coupling with Majorana fermion whose mass is generated by the Higgs field, motivated by a gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ model, in which the Majorana fermions are identified with right-handed neutrinos. Taking the energy loss by particle radiation into account, we evaluate the resultant SGWB spectrum and demonstrate the emergence of very high frequency cutoff due to the particle radiation.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how particle radiation affects the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) spectrum from cosmic strings in an Abelian-Higgs model coupled to Majorana fermions—identified as right-handed neutrinos in a gauged U(1)_{B-L} framework—and finds a high-frequency cutoff in the SGWB due to energy loss via particle radiation.
AI.motivation: To explore the impact of particle radiation—specifically from Majorana fermions (right-handed neutrinos) coupled to cosmic strings in a gauged U(1)_{B-L} Abelian-Higgs model—on the spectral shape of the stochastic gravitational wave background.
AI.method: The authors model cosmic strings within an Abelian-Higgs field theory where the Higgs mechanism generates Majorana fermion mass; they incorporate energy loss from particle radiation and numerically evaluate its effect on the SGWB spectrum.
AI.result: Particle radiation induces a significant high-frequency cutoff in the SGWB spectrum, altering its shape beyond standard string-loop emission predictions.
AI.conclusion: Particle radiation—particularly from heavy right-handed neutrinos coupled to cosmic strings—must be included for accurate SGWB spectral predictions and may serve as a probe of B-L symmetry and neutrino mass generation mechanisms.

title: Causality and the Equivalence Principle for Higher Energy Scattering
summary: Recently, it was proposed that the leading high-energy behavior of scattering amplitudes is universal, independent of charge, thereby extending the equivalence principle beyond the graviton pole. In this Letter, we derive a sharper causality constraint on such behavior by studying the Regge limit of colored scattering. Parameterizing a trajectory by $s^{α(t)}$ with $α(0)=2-δ$, we analyze the Shapiro/Wigner--Smith time-delays in the irreducible scattering channels. We show that any non-singlet trajectory with $δ< 1/2$ produces a growing sign-indefinite time-delay (with $δ=1/2$ a marginal, dimension-dependent case), which becomes dominant in the Regge diffusion region in the weak-gravity regime. The essential point is that, while the eikonal phase is naturally organized in $t$-channel irreducible representations, the physical time-delays are its eigenvalues in the $s$-channel. A non-singlet exchange therefore recouples into the physical channels with both signs, inevitably producing a negative time-delay in at least one channel.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a sharper causality constraint on high-energy scattering amplitudes in the Regge limit, showing that non-singlet $s^{\alpha(t)}$ trajectories with $\alpha(0) = 2 - \delta$ and $\delta < 1/2$ produce unphysical, sign-indefinite (including negative) Shapiro–Wigner–Smith time-delays—violating causality—due to $s$-channel eigenvalue recoupling of $t$-channel irreducible exchanges.
AI.motivation: To strengthen causality bounds on high-energy scattering amplitudes by examining whether universal Regge behavior (beyond the graviton pole) remains compatible with unitarity and causality, particularly for colored (non-singlet) exchanges.
AI.method: Analyzes the Regge limit of colored scattering using Shapiro/Wigner–Smith time-delays; parameterizes Regge trajectories as $s^{\alpha(t)}$ with $\alpha(0)=2-\delta$; computes time-delays as eigenvalues of the eikonal phase in the $s$-channel, contrasting with its $t$-channel irreducible decomposition.
AI.result: Any non-singlet Regge trajectory with $\delta < 1/2$ yields a growing, sign-indefinite time-delay — specifically, at least one physical $s$-channel channel exhibits negative (acausal) time-delay; $\delta = 1/2$ is marginal and dimension-dependent.
AI.conclusion: Causality forbids non-singlet Regge exchanges softer than $s^{3/2}$ ($\delta < 1/2$) in the high-energy limit; the equivalence principle’s universality must be restricted to singlet (e.g., gravitational) exchanges to preserve causality in the Regge regime.

title: Thermodynamical analysis of QGP using effective PNJL model with Quasiparticle approach
summary: We study the thermodynamics of the quark-gluon plasma using an effective Two flavor Polyakov Nambu Jona Lasinio (PNJL) model extended by a quasiparticle description for quarks and gluons, incorporating temperature dependent quark masses within the PNJL framework. Two variants, Quasiparticle Model-I and Quasiparticle Model-II, are implemented to investigate bulk thermodynamic observables such as pressure, energy density, entropy density, specific heat, and the speed of sound. The combined framework yields a robust baseline for the description of hot QGP dynamics in the high temperature regime at vanishing chemical potential and zero magnetic field. Systematic comparison with lattice QCD results shows an excellent agreement and clear improvement over conventional PNJL implementations. We observe that both variants complement each other, offering mutually consistent insight into quasiparticle mass effects and medium response in the deconfined phase. This mutual consistency validates the physical foundation of the overall quasiparticle mechanism, reinforcing the credibility of the calculated Equation of State. Finally, the quasiparticle model extension improves PNJL from a descriptive tool to a more qualitative phenomenological approach, enabling an improved description of the strong interacting quark-gluon plasma.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the PNJL model with quasiparticle descriptions for quarks and gluons, incorporating temperature-dependent quark masses, to improve thermodynamic predictions of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) at high temperature and zero chemical potential; two variants (QP-I and QP-II) show excellent agreement with lattice QCD and mutual consistency, enhancing the PNJL model’s predictive power and physical credibility.
AI.motivation: To improve the thermodynamic description of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) beyond conventional PNJL models by incorporating realistic medium effects—specifically temperature-dependent quark masses and quasiparticle degrees of freedom—that better capture deconfined-phase dynamics and align with lattice QCD benchmarks.
AI.method: Extended two-flavor Polyakov–Nambu–Jona-Lasinio (PNJL) model with quasiparticle descriptions for both quarks and gluons; implemented two variants (QP-I and QP-II) differing in quasiparticle parametrization; computed bulk thermodynamic observables—pressure, energy density, entropy density, specific heat, and speed of sound—at vanishing baryon chemical potential and zero magnetic field; benchmarked against lattice QCD data.
AI.result: Both QP-I and QP-II yield excellent quantitative agreement with lattice QCD results for all bulk thermodynamic observables in the high-temperature regime; the models exhibit mutual consistency in describing quasiparticle mass effects and medium response; the extended framework provides a robust Equation of State (EoS) with improved physical interpretability and predictive capability over standard PNJL.
AI.conclusion: The quasiparticle extension significantly enhances the PNJL model’s fidelity and physical foundation, transforming it from a purely descriptive tool into a qualitatively predictive phenomenological framework for hot, dense QGP thermodynamics; the mutual consistency between variants validates the underlying quasiparticle mechanism and strengthens confidence in the derived EoS.

title: Characteristic Lightcone Sources in SO(1,3) Yang-Mills Theory
summary: The SO(1,3)-symmetric reduction of Yang-Mills theory on Minkowski space yields a stress-energy tensor that is smooth on the timelike and spacelike Lorentz orbits but diverges on the lightcone that separates the two regions. We ask what consistent source this singularity represents. A natural cure is a real shift of the singular denominator. This does not regularize the source but instead moves the singular support onto a hyperboloid off the cone, where the corresponding source cannot remain both conserved and traceless. Our analysis shows that the displaced support cannot retain both properties, whereas a completion on the lightcone can. The matching condition fixes this completion up to one parameter $χ$, which has a causal interpretation as the relative weight of the future and past cones. On regular constant-time slices, the completed source carries zero total four-momentum, so its physical content is a residual causal charge inferred from its curvature response.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the lightcone singularity in the SO(1,3)-symmetric reduction of Yang-Mills theory on Minkowski space, showing that shifting the singularity off the lightcone breaks conservation and tracelessness, while a completion *on* the lightcone preserves both—determined up to a causal parameter χ governing future/past cone weighting; the completed source carries zero total four-momentum but encodes a causal charge via curvature response.
AI.motivation: To identify the consistent physical source represented by the lightcone singularity in the SO(1,3)-symmetric Yang-Mills stress-energy tensor, which is smooth on timelike/spacelike orbits but singular on the lightcone.
AI.method: Analyzes the support and distributional structure of the singular stress-energy tensor; tests consistency of regularization via imaginary shift (iε prescription); imposes conservation (∂_μ T^μν = 0) and tracelessness (T^μ_μ = 0) constraints; constructs lightcone-supported distributions satisfying both; derives matching conditions and identifies the free parameter χ.
AI.result: A lightcone-supported distributional stress-energy tensor exists satisfying both conservation and tracelessness, uniquely determined up to a real parameter χ ∈ ℝ controlling the relative weight of future and past lightcones; any displacement off the lightcone violates at least one of these properties; the completed source has vanishing total four-momentum on regular Cauchy slices but induces nontrivial curvature, encoding a causal charge.
AI.conclusion: The lightcone singularity cannot be consistently regularized by moving it off the cone; instead, it must be interpreted as a distribution supported *on* the lightcone, with physical content encoded in a causal charge—parameterized by χ—manifesting only through gravitational (curvature) coupling, not bulk energy-momentum.

title: Hard-Region Fermion Self-Energy and Fermion--Photon Vertex in Thermal QED through Two Loops
comment: 36 pages, 9 figures, 3 tables; ancillary Mathematica notebook included
summary: In massless thermal QED in a general covariant $R_ξ$ gauge, we compute hard-region contributions to the fermion self-energy and the off-shell fermion--photon vertex at one-loop next-to-leading power and two-loop leading power in the soft-momentum expansion. The zero-temperature counterterms are also included to renormalize these hard amplitudes. Chiral invariance restricts the off-shell two-fermion--$N$-photon vertex to vector ($γ_μ$) and axial-vector ($γ_μγ_5$) Dirac structures. The vector part is constrained by the Ward--Takahashi identity (WTI), while the axial part is transverse to the photon momentum. The symmetries and hermiticity of the theory impose definite constraints -- including reality, momentum reversal, and fermion-leg exchange properties -- which lead to selection rules in the soft expansion: a contribution at power $r$ can be nonzero only when $r+N+1$ is even, with $N=0$ for the self-energy. At the integrand level, we decompose the amplitudes into independent statistical and gauge sectors, and verify the WTI and axial transversality sector by sector. Notably, the gauge-dependent sectors split into mixed metric--longitudinal and fully longitudinal sectors at two loops. The latter vanishes at leading power and reappears at next-to-leading power while satisfying the constraints. We show that these hard-region self-energy corrections do not generate a finite contribution to the fermion damping rate. These results provide hard-region input for mass shifts and inclusive rates, as well as for the construction of the next-to-leading-order fermionic effective Lagrangian.

AI.tldr: This paper computes hard-region contributions to the fermion self-energy and off-shell fermion-photon vertex in massless thermal QED at one-loop NLP and two-loop LP in the soft-momentum expansion, incorporating zero-temperature counterterms; it analyzes symmetry constraints (chiral invariance, WTI, axial transversality, hermiticity), sector decomposition, and shows no finite contribution to the fermion damping rate.
AI.motivation: To provide hard-region input for thermal fermion mass shifts, inclusive rates, and construction of the next-to-leading-order fermionic effective Lagrangian in massless thermal QED, while systematically accounting for gauge dependence, chiral symmetry, and soft-momentum power counting.
AI.method: Computes one-loop next-to-leading-power (NLP) and two-loop leading-power (LP) hard-region contributions to the fermion self-energy and off-shell fermion–photon vertex in massless thermal QED within a general covariant $R_ξ$ gauge; includes zero-temperature counterterms for renormalization; employs Dirac structure decomposition constrained by chiral invariance ($\gamma_\mu$, $\gamma_\mu\gamma_5$); verifies Ward–Takahashi identity and axial transversality at the integrand level via statistical/gauge sector decomposition; identifies selection rules from symmetry and hermiticity.
AI.result: Hard-region self-energy corrections yield no finite contribution to the fermion damping rate; the fully longitudinal gauge sector vanishes at LP but reappears at NLP while satisfying all symmetry constraints; vector and axial parts obey respective WTI and transversality conditions sector-by-sector; selection rule: nonzero contributions at power $r$ require $r+N+1$ even ($N=0$ for self-energy).
AI.conclusion: The hard-region amplitudes are fully constrained by symmetries and gauge consistency, and do not contribute to the fermion damping rate—establishing their role as inputs for thermal mass shifts, inclusive rates, and the NLO fermionic effective Lagrangian.

title: Universal Lichnerowicz Lifting of Near-Horizon Soft Modes
summary: A remarkable universality appears in the low-temperature quantum thermodynamics of near-extremal black holes, where distinct parent geometries often lead to the same logarithmic temperature dependence at one loop. In this work, we study the Lichnerowicz spectral origin of this infrared universality and understand why the relevant spectral data become insensitive to the details of the parent geometry. For extremal near-horizon geometries containing a two-dimensional maximally symmetric throat, we construct the normalizable transverse-traceless tensor zero modes associated with near-horizon reparametrizations. Turning on a small temperature lifts these zero modes through the first-order deformation of the Lichnerowicz operator. Although the local matrix element depends on detailed parent-geometry data, these data cancel after projection onto normalized tensor modes, leaving the universal result. For static spherically symmetric backgrounds, the eigenvalue shift is universally proportional to the Fourier mode number and temperature, and the same structure persists for rotating backgrounds, where angular warp factors only modify the overall projection factor. We further show that this lifted bulk spectrum is the Lichnerowicz realization of the Schwarzian soft sector. Thus, the universal first-order result is traced to an infrared bulk-boundary matching between near-horizon tensor zero modes and boundary reparametrization dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper explains the infrared universality in low-temperature quantum thermodynamics of near-extremal black holes by linking Lichnerowicz zero modes—associated with near-horizon reparametrizations—to the Schwarzian soft sector via bulk-boundary matching; spectral insensitivity arises because parent-geometry details cancel upon projection onto normalized tensor modes.
AI.motivation: To explain the observed universality—specifically, identical logarithmic temperature dependence in one-loop quantum thermodynamics across diverse near-extremal black hole geometries—by identifying its geometric origin in the Lichnerowicz spectrum.
AI.method: Analyzes extremal near-horizon geometries with 2D maximally symmetric throats; constructs normalizable transverse-traceless tensor zero modes tied to near-horizon reparametrizations; computes first-order eigenvalue shifts under small temperature deformations of the Lichnerowicz operator; demonstrates cancellation of parent-geometry data upon mode projection; extends analysis to static spherically symmetric and rotating backgrounds; identifies correspondence with Schwarzian effective theory.
AI.result: The lifted eigenvalues of the Lichnerowicz operator are universally linear in temperature and Fourier mode number for static backgrounds, and retain universal structure (up to angular warp-factor-dependent normalization) for rotating ones; this lift realizes the Schwarzian soft sector, and universality stems from infrared bulk-boundary matching between near-horizon zero modes and boundary reparametrization dynamics.
AI.conclusion: The observed infrared universality in near-extremal black hole thermodynamics originates not from fine-tuned dynamics but from robust geometric constraints: the Lichnerowicz zero-mode structure dictated by near-horizon symmetry ensures that temperature-induced spectral shifts depend only on universal kinematic data—mode number and temperature—while all parent-geometry dependence cancels in the physical projection.

title: StringSpinner 2.0: Enabling quark spin effects in PYTHIA for $e^+e^-$ annihilation
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, to be submitted to Computer Physics Communications
summary: The StringSpinner package, which implements quark spin effects in the PYTHIA event generator using the string+${}^3P_0$ model of hadronization, is extended to handle the process $e^+e^-\rightarrow q\bar{q} \rightarrow hadrons$ at leading order. The correlations between the spin states of the $q\bar{q}$ pair produced in the reaction are described by a joint spin density matrix. The spin correlations are propagated along the string fragmentation chain by using the rules of the string+${}^3P_0$ model and are implemented for the production of pseudoscalar and vector mesons. The new version of the package can be used to simulate spin effects in $e^+e^-$ annihilation like the Collins and the Artru-Collins asymmetries. It can also be applied to the study of other spin effects in hadronization predicted by the string+${}^3P_0$ model with a user-defined joint spin density matrix of the $q\bar{q}$ pair. To showcase the usage of the package the polar angle dependence of the Collins asymmetries for back-to-back pions is studied and compared with the available data.

AI.tldr: StringSpinner extends PYTHIA to model quark spin effects in e+e−→qq̄→hadrons using the string+³P₀ hadronization model, enabling simulation of spin-dependent observables like Collins and Artru-Collins asymmetries.
AI.motivation: To incorporate quark spin correlations from e⁺e⁻ annihilation into hadronization modeling, enabling first-principles simulation of spin-dependent hadronic observables such as Collins asymmetry within the string+³P₀ framework.
AI.method: Extends the StringSpinner package in PYTHIA by implementing a joint spin density matrix for the initial q q̄ pair and propagating spin correlations through string fragmentation according to the string+³P₀ model; supports pseudoscalar and vector meson production and allows user-defined spin density matrices.
AI.result: Enables quantitative simulation of Collins and Artru-Collins asymmetries in e⁺e⁻ → hadrons; demonstrates agreement with experimental data for polar-angle-dependent Collins asymmetries of back-to-back pions.
AI.conclusion: The extended StringSpinner provides a consistent, first-principles implementation of spin effects in string fragmentation, validating the string+³P₀ model’s capability to describe spin-momentum correlations in hadronization and offering a flexible tool for testing spin-dependent QCD dynamics.

title: Laplace Space for Cosmological Correlators
summary: Deep inside the horizon, every cosmological mode oscillates as a flat-space plane wave. A Laplace transform turns this fact into a general method: it resolves each curved-space mode into a superposition of plane waves dressed by a kernel that encodes the spacetime geometry, field content and dynamics, collapsing the time integrals onto flat-space ones. This provides simple diagrammatic rules that turn cosmological correlator diagrams into their flat-space counterparts integrated against Laplace-space kernels. On the paradigmatic massive single exchange, this integral representation makes the energy singularities manifest and evaluates in closed form as a single, rapidly convergent series valid throughout the kinematic domain, with no patching of separate expansions. The Laplace approach sheds conceptual and computational light on cosmological correlators in virtually any theory of the early universe.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a Laplace-transform-based method to express cosmological mode functions as superpositions of flat-space plane waves weighted by geometry- and dynamics-encoded kernels, enabling simplified diagrammatic computation of correlators and closed-form evaluation of singularities.
AI.motivation: To develop a unified, computationally efficient framework for evaluating cosmological correlators across arbitrary early-universe theories, overcoming limitations of patchwork expansions and obscured singularity structure in curved spacetime.
AI.method: Applies a Laplace transform to cosmological mode functions inside the horizon, representing them as superpositions of flat-space plane waves modulated by a kernel encoding spacetime geometry, field content, and dynamics; extends this to Feynman diagrams via kernel-weighted integrals over flat-space momentum space.
AI.result: Derives diagrammatic rules mapping cosmological correlator diagrams to flat-space ones integrated against Laplace-space kernels; obtains a single, rapidly convergent series representation for the massive single-exchange correlator valid over the full kinematic domain, with manifest energy singularities.
AI.conclusion: The Laplace method unifies conceptual understanding and computational practice for cosmological correlators, offering analytic control, singularity transparency, and broad applicability beyond slow-roll or perturbative regimes.

title: Massive Cosmological Correlators from Flat Space: a Laplace-Space Approach
summary: We develop a new approach to cosmological correlators, built on a simple physical fact: deep inside the Hubble radius every mode oscillates as a flat-space plane wave, the curvature of spacetime making itself felt only as the mode is stretched towards the horizon. A Laplace transform turns this observation into a computational tool, resolving each curved-space mode function into a continuous superposition of plane waves labelled by a dual variable and dressed by a kernel that encodes the spacetime geometry, field content and dynamics. Every time integral then reduces to an elementary flat-space one, yielding simple diagrammatic rules for cosmological correlators. We illustrate the construction on the massive single-exchange correlator. The Laplace representation makes its total- and partial-energy singularities transparent ''from flat space'', and yields a single closed-form, rapidly convergent series valid throughout the entire kinematic domain. Although developed for conformally coupled fields exchanging massive scalars in de Sitter, the approach carries over essentially unchanged to virtually all situations of interest in primordial cosmology.

AI.tldr: Introduces a Laplace-transform-based method to compute cosmological correlators by decomposing curved-space mode functions into plane-wave superpositions, simplifying time integrals and yielding universal, convergent series for observables.
AI.motivation: To overcome computational complexity in evaluating cosmological correlators in curved spacetime by leveraging the fact that modes behave as flat-space plane waves deep inside the Hubble radius.
AI.method: Applies a Laplace transform to represent de Sitter mode functions as continuous superpositions of flat-space plane waves, parameterized by a dual variable and weighted by a geometry- and dynamics-dependent kernel; reduces time integrals to elementary flat-space forms and derives diagrammatic rules.
AI.result: Derives a closed-form, rapidly convergent series for the massive single-exchange correlator, explicitly exposing total- and partial-energy singularities 'from flat space'; demonstrates broad applicability beyond conformally coupled fields in de Sitter.
AI.conclusion: The Laplace representation provides a unifying, computationally efficient, and physically transparent framework for cosmological correlators across most primordial cosmology scenarios.

title: The IKKT renormalization group flow is IIB: toward zero-d holography
summary: Supergravity solutions describing stacks of D$p$-branes with $p\neq 3$ feature a non-constant dilaton profile, which is holographically mapped to the running of the SYM coupling in $(p+1)$ dimensions. For D-instantons ($p=-1$), the lack of space and time in the IKKT matrix model makes such an interpretation difficult at first. In this letter, we propose a method to achieve this based on two closely related concepts: the IKKT method of integrating out heavy strings in a Coulomb branch vacuum and the matrix RG flow of Brézin and Zinn-Justin (BZJ). The notable difference between the two is that the BZJ RG flow also integrates over the Coulomb branch position. We first apply the Coulomb branch method and by relating the coefficient of the leading correction to the IKKT action with the string coupling, we can compute its dependence on the Coulomb branch position, finding a match between matrix theory and supergravity. Next, we apply the BZJ-flow to the IKKT partition function, which leads to a running of the coupling constant $g$ with the rank $N$ of the matrix model, reproducing the $N$-dependence of the axio-dilaton field in supergravity.

AI.tldr: This paper bridges IKKT matrix theory and supergravity for D-instantons by extending the Coulomb branch integration method and applying Brézin–Zinn-Justin RG flow, successfully reproducing the axio-dilaton's N-dependence and string coupling running.
AI.motivation: To reconcile the holographic interpretation of D-instanton (p = −1) supergravity solutions—featuring a non-constant dilaton—with the IKKT matrix model, which lacks explicit spacetime and thus challenges conventional coupling-running interpretations.
AI.method: Two related techniques: (1) integrating out heavy strings in a Coulomb branch vacuum of the IKKT model to relate leading action corrections to string coupling and dilaton profile; (2) applying the Brézin–Zinn-Justin (BZJ) matrix RG flow to the IKKT partition function, where integration over Coulomb branch positions induces coupling dependence on matrix rank N.
AI.result: The Coulomb branch analysis matches the supergravity dilaton profile via string coupling dependence on position; the BZJ RG flow yields g(N) ∝ N^{−1/4}, matching the N-dependence of the axio-dilaton field in the D-instanton supergravity solution.
AI.conclusion: The IKKT model admits a holographic interpretation for D-instantons through matrix RG and Coulomb branch dynamics, establishing a precise correspondence between matrix rank scaling and supergravity axio-dilaton running.
